### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# Node.js Inspect Debugger

## Overview

When `console.log` isn't enough, drive Node's built-in V8 inspector programmatically from the terminal. You get real breakpoints, step in/over/out, call-stack walking, local/closure scope dumps, and arbitrary expression evaluation in the paused frame.

Two tools, pick one:

- **`node inspect`** — built-in, zero install, CLI REPL. Best for quick poking.
- **`ndb` / CDP via `chrome-remote-interface`** — scriptable from Node/Python; best when you want to automate many breakpoints, collect state across runs, or debug non-interactively from an agent loop.

**Prefer `node inspect` first.** It's always available and the REPL is fast.

## When to Use

- A Node test fails and you need to see intermediate state
- ui-tui crashes or behaves wrong and you want to inspect React/Ink state pre-render
- tui_gateway child processes (`_SlashWorker`, PTY bridge workers) misbehave
- You need to inspect a value in a closure that `console.log` can't reach without patching
- Perf: attach to a running process to capture a CPU profile or heap snapshot

**Don't use for:** things `console.log` solves in under a minute. Breakpoint-driven debugging is heavier; use it when the payoff is real.

## Quick Reference: `node inspect` REPL

Launch paused on first line:

```bash
node inspect path/to/script.js
# or with tsx
node --inspect-brk $(which tsx) path/to/script.ts
```

The `debug>` prompt accepts:

| Command | Action |
|---|---|
| `c` or `cont` | continue |
| `n` or `next` | step over |
| `s` or `step` | step into |
| `o` or `out` | step out |
| `pause` | pause running code |
| `sb('file.js', 42)` | set breakpoint at file.js line 42 |
| `sb(42)` | set breakpoint at line 42 of current file |
| `sb('functionName')` | break when function is called |
| `cb('file.js', 42)` | clear breakpoint |
| `breakpoints` | list all breakpoints |
| `bt` | backtrace (call stack) |
| `list(5)` | show 5 lines of source around current position |
| `watch('expr')` | evaluate expr on every pause |
| `watchers` | show watched expressions |
| `repl` | drop into REPL in current scope (Ctrl+C to exit REPL) |
| `exec expr` | evaluate expression once |
| `restart` | restart script |
| `kill` | kill the script |
| `.exit` | quit debugger |

**In the `repl` sub-mode:** type any JS expression, including access to locals/closure variables. `Ctrl+C` exits back to `debug>`.

## Attaching to a Running Process

When the process is already running (e.g. a long-lived dev server or the TUI gateway):

```bash
# 1. Send SIGUSR1 to enable the inspector on an existing process
kill -SIGUSR1 <pid>
# Node prints: Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:9229/<uuid>

# 2. Attach the debugger CLI
node inspect -p <pid>
# or by URL
node inspect ws://127.0.0.1:9229/<uuid>
```

To start a process with the inspector from the beginning:

```bash
node --inspect script.js           # listen on 127.0.0.1:9229, keep running
node --inspect-brk script.js       # listen AND pause on first line
node --inspect=0.0.0.0:9230 script.js   # custom host:port
```

For TypeScript via tsx:

```bash
node --inspect-brk --import tsx script.ts
# or older tsx
node --inspect-brk -r tsx/cjs script.ts
```

## Programmatic CDP (scripting from terminal)

When you want to automate — set many breakpoints, capture scope state, script a repro — use `chrome-remote-interface`:

```bash
npm i -g chrome-remote-interface        # or project-local
# Start your target:
node --inspect-brk=9229 target.js &
```

Driver script (save as `~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cdp-debug.js`):

```javascript
const CDP = require('chrome-remote-interface');

(async () => {
  const client = await CDP({ port: 9229 });
  const { Debugger, Runtime } = client;

  Debugger.paused(async ({ callFrames, reason }) => {
    const top = callFrames[0];
    console.log(`PAUSED: ${reason} @ ${top.url}:${top.location.lineNumber + 1}`);

    // Walk scopes for locals
    for (const scope of top.scopeChain) {
      if (scope.type === 'local' || scope.type === 'closure') {
        const { result } = await Runtime.getProperties({
          objectId: scope.object.objectId,
          ownProperties: true,
        });
        for (const p of result) {
          console.log(`  ${scope.type}.${p.name} =`, p.value?.value ?? p.value?.description);
        }
      }
    }

    // Evaluate an expression in the paused frame
    const { result } = await Debugger.evaluateOnCallFrame({
      callFrameId: top.callFrameId,
      expression: 'typeof state !== "undefined" ? JSON.stringify(state) : "n/a"',
    });
    console.log('state =', result.value ?? result.description);

    await Debugger.resume();
  });

  await Runtime.enable();
  await Debugger.enable();

  // Set a breakpoint by URL regex + line
  await Debugger.setBreakpointByUrl({
    urlRegex: '.*app\\.tsx$',
    lineNumber: 119,       // 0-indexed
    columnNumber: 0,
  });

  await Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger();
})();
```

Run it:

```bash
node ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cdp-debug.js
```

Hermes-specific note: `chrome-remote-interface` is NOT in `ui-tui/package.json`. Install it to a throwaway location if you don't want to dirty the project:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cdp-tools && cd ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cdp-tools && npm i chrome-remote-interface
NODE_PATH=~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cdp-tools/node_modules node ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cdp-debug.js
```

## Debugging Hermes ui-tui

The TUI is built Ink + tsx. Two common scenarios:

### Debugging a single Ink component under dev

`ui-tui/package.json` has `npm run dev` (tsx --watch). Add `--inspect-brk` by running tsx directly:

```bash
cd <hermes-agent-repo>/ui-tui
npm run build    # produce dist/ once so transpile isn't needed on first load
node --inspect-brk dist/entry.js
# In another terminal:
node inspect -p <node pid>
```

Then inside `debug>`:

```
sb('dist/app.js', 220)     # or wherever the suspect render is
cont
```

When it pauses, `repl` → inspect `props`, state refs, `useInput` handler values, etc.

### Debugging a running `hermes --tui`

The TUI spawns Node from the Python CLI. Easiest path:

```bash
# 1. Launch TUI
hermes --tui &
TUI_PID=$(pgrep -f 'ui-tui/dist/entry' | head -1)

# 2. Enable inspector on that Node PID
kill -SIGUSR1 "$TUI_PID"

# 3. Find the WS URL
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9229/json/list | jq -r '.[0].webSocketDebuggerUrl'

# 4. Attach
node inspect ws://127.0.0.1:9229/<uuid>
```

Interacting with the TUI (typing in its window) continues to advance execution; your debugger can pause it on a breakpoint at any `sb(...)`.

### Debugging `_SlashWorker` / PTY child processes

Those are Python, not Node — use the `python-debugpy` skill for them. Only Node portions (Ink UI, tui_gateway client, tsx-run tests under `ui-tui/`) use this skill.

## Running Vitest Tests Under the Debugger

```bash
cd <hermes-agent-repo>/ui-tui
# Run a single test file paused on entry
node --inspect-brk ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --no-file-parallelism src/app/foo.test.tsx
```

In another terminal: `node inspect -p <pid>`, then `sb('src/app/foo.tsx', 42)`, `cont`.

Use `--no-file-parallelism` (vitest) or `--runInBand` (jest) so only one worker exists — debugging a pool is painful.

## Heap Snapshots & CPU Profiles (Non-interactive)

From the CDP driver above, swap Debugger for `HeapProfiler` / `Profiler`:

```javascript
// CPU profile for 5 seconds
await client.Profiler.enable();
await client.Profiler.start();
await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 5000));
const { profile } = await client.Profiler.stop();
require('fs').writeFileSync('~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cpu.cpuprofile', JSON.stringify(profile));
// Open ~/.hermes/cache/scratch/cpu.cpuprofile in Chrome DevTools → Performance tab
```

```javascript
// Heap snapshot
await client.HeapProfiler.enable();
const chunks = [];
client.HeapProfiler.addHeapSnapshotChunk(({ chunk }) => chunks.push(chunk));
await client.HeapProfiler.takeHeapSnapshot({ reportProgress: false });
require('fs').writeFileSync('~/.hermes/cache/scratch/heap.heapsnapshot', chunks.join(''));
```

## Common Pitfalls

1. **Wrong line numbers in TS source.** Breakpoints hit the emitted JS, not the `.ts`. Either (a) break in the built `dist/*.js`, or (b) enable sourcemaps (`node --enable-source-maps`) and use `sb('src/app.tsx', N)` — but only with CDP clients that follow sourcemaps. `node inspect` CLI does not.

2. **`--inspect` vs `--inspect-brk`.** `--inspect` starts the inspector but doesn't pause; your script races past your first breakpoint if you attach too late. Use `--inspect-brk` when you need to set breakpoints before any code runs.

3. **Port collisions.** Default is `9229`. If multiple Node processes are inspecting, pass `--inspect=0` (random port) and read the actual URL from `/json/list`:
   ```bash
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9229/json/list   # lists all inspectable targets on the host
   ```

4. **Child processes.** `--inspect` on a parent does NOT inspect its children. Use `NODE_OPTIONS='--inspect-brk' node parent.js` to propagate to every child; be aware they all need unique ports (Node auto-increments when `NODE_OPTIONS='--inspect'` is inherited).

5. **Background kills.** If you `Ctrl+C` out of `node inspect` while the target is paused, the target stays paused. Either `cont` first, or `kill` the target explicitly.

6. **Running `node inspect` through an agent terminal.** It's a PTY-friendly REPL. In Hermes, launch it with `terminal(pty=true)` or `background=true` + `process(action='submit', data='...')`. Non-PTY foreground mode will work for one-shot commands but not for interactive stepping.

7. **Security.** `--inspect=0.0.0.0:9229` exposes arbitrary code execution. Always bind to `127.0.0.1` (the default) unless you have an isolated network.

## Verification Checklist

After setting up a debug session, verify:

- [ ] `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9229/json/list` returns exactly the target you expect
- [ ] First breakpoint actually hits (if it doesn't, you likely missed `--inspect-brk` or attached after execution completed)
- [ ] Source listing at pause shows the right file (mismatch = sourcemap issue, see pitfall 1)
- [ ] `exec process.pid` in `repl` returns the PID you meant to attach to

## One-Shot Recipes

**"Why is this variable undefined at line X?"**
```bash
node --inspect-brk script.js &
node inspect -p $!
# debug>
sb('script.js', X)
cont
# paused. Now:
repl
> myVariable
> Object.keys(this)
```

**"What's the call path into this function?"**
```
debug> sb('suspectFn')
debug> cont
# paused on entry
debug> bt
```

**"This async chain hangs — where?"**
```
# Start with --inspect (no -brk), let it run to the hang, then:
debug> pause
debug> bt
# Now you see the stuck frame
```

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# PHP Code Audit

Audit a PHP web app for **real user-facing bugs**, not style nits. The task is READ-ONLY — the deliverable is the report, never edits. (If the caller asked for structural review too, cover code quality/perf in the same pass.)

## When to use
- "Audit / find bugs / review a PHP app" with focus areas like quota counting, subscription expiry, payment validation, delete cascade, N+1, PHP 8 warnings.
- Pre-rewrite or pre-migration QA of a custom-framework codebase.
- Any PHP app with controllers/models/views plus a schema.sql (and migration files).

## Workflow (order matters — feature code comes last)
1. **Inventory**: every `.php` file, `.htaccess`, `database/*.sql`. Read the entry point (`index.php`) first: `spl_autoload_register` paths, the router table (your map of every endpoint), `APP_URL`/base-dir handling (sub-folder installs).
2. **Core layer**: config, PDO wrapper (`Database`), `Auth` (session/CSRF/throttling), `helpers` (`e()`, date conversion, numbers). Note PHP-version gates: `str_starts_with`/`str_contains`, arrow fns, typed properties ⇒ PHP ≥ 8.0 — check whether README declares a minimum.
3. **Models**: read all models; flag raw SQL string interpolation (LIMIT from constants is fine; interpolated values are not). For billing/subscription models, trace every state method: `validate()`, `isActive()`, `getQuota()`, `consume()`, `activate()`.
4. **Controllers (user + admin)**: walk each full flow: auth gate → CSRF → feature/quota check → write (transaction?) → consumption → redirect. Admin controllers often duplicate user flows minus the owner-scoping (`WHERE user_id`) — compare the pairs deliberately.
5. **Views**: skim only where SQL/loops live — dashboards, list tables, invoice/print layouts. Look for per-row queries (N+1), duplicated model re-instantiation inside views, client-side gating (html2canvas/jspdf "downloads"), CDN assets without local fallback, inline JSON-data scripts.
6. **Schema**: read `schema.sql` AND every `migration_*.sql` — drift between them is the classic "fresh install works, upgrade breaks" failure. Check FKs (CASCADE can silently erase audit history when a parent is deleted), missing indexes on `user_id`/`status`, VARCHAR dates, DECIMAL money returning as strings.
7. **Verify each candidate bug is reachable**: exact route in router, method runs, SQL executes. Never cite a bug you did not trace end-to-end.

## Report format (the expected deliverable shape)
- Per issue: **severity — file:line — code snippet — fix**.
- Sections: Logic bugs (user-visible) → Code quality → Performance → PHP 8 compat → **prioritized fix list** at the end.
- Lead the summary with outcomes; bullets; don't replay the process.
- Separate *intended design* from *bug*: read UI text (JS modals, form help text) and schema comments before calling something a bug. If the app deliberately warns "this edit consumes quota", call it a design/UX problem with consequences, not a typo.
- If no PHP runtime is available, say "static analysis only" explicitly.

## Checkpoints — where bugs actually live
- **Quota/limit flows**: is the check on BOTH create and update? Does update also consume quota? Does delete refund? Is check→increment atomic (TOCTOU/double-submit race)? Are counters reset per calendar month in the app timezone?
- **Billing/expiry**: is active state the stored `status` column (goes stale after end_date) vs computed `end_date >= CURDATE()`? Anything auto-flipping status at expiry? Does renewal extend from `end_date` while still valid?
- **Money**: totals are DECIMAL(18,0) returned as strings — watch float casts, number_format; a line discount bigger than the line total silently clamps to 0.
- **Dates/i18n**: does the app store a user-typed Shamsi string straight into VARCHAR with no validation? Does the Jalali→Gregorian parser handle Persian digits?
- **Deletion**: entity delete — FK CASCADE vs explicit child cleanup; does deleting a user/plan destroy audit/history rows or leave orphans?
- **Perf**: count queries per page — layouts re-instantiating models, duplicate getFeatures()/isActive() calls; a per-request static cache is the standard fix. Missing indexes on (user_id, status) for payment tables.

## Critical pitfalls (learned the hard way)
- **Persian digits silently become 0**: `intval('Persian')` ⇒ 0. Any Jalali/Gregorian helper parsing user input **must strip Persian-Persian (Persian) and Persian-Persian (Arabic) digits to ASCII before intval**. Failure mode: a null date silently saved — a paid plan with NULL end_date is then treated as FREE (user paid, features locked, no error anywhere).
- **Check-then-act races**: `if (remaining > 0) { insert; increment }` lets double-click/double-submit exceed the quota. Atomic single-UPDATE (`SET used = used + 1 WHERE used < limit`) is the fix.
- **Stale status columns**: tables keep `status='active'` long past `end_date`; always gate on computed date logic, treat the column as display-only.
- **Discount codes**: consumed at *submission* — burns max_uses coupons even when the payment is later REJECTED. Correct site: increment the code at admin approval; refund/decrement on rejection.
- **"Premium" gates in JS** (PDF/PNG via browser libs) are not enforcement — browser Print always wins. Server endpoints must re-check the plan.
- **PHP 8 gates**: `str_starts_with` in the router means PHP ≥ 8.0 required; on a 7.4 host it is a white-screen on every page. Check what minimum PHP the README declares.
- **Migration drift**: schema.sql may be newer than migration files; `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` only on MySQL 8.0.29+/MariaDB — older DBs die in migrate.

## Tooling notes (Windows/git-bash)
- `read_file` may misclassify UTF-8 PHP with Persian/RTL comments as "Binary". Verify the file type with `file foo.php`; if it is Unicode text, read via `nl -ba foo.php` in the terminal tool.
- Batch reads: controllers in parallel first, then models, then views. Grep for SQL queries and view loops instead of reading whole files.
- Sample lint sweep: `for f in $(find . -name '*.php'); do php -l "$f"; done` only if a php binary exists; otherwise say static-only.

## Support files
- `references/php-audit-bug-catalogue.md` — annotated catalogue of recurring bug patterns with sample/fix recipes (from a real audit of a Persian invoice SaaS).


### 📚 Auxiliary References, Templates & Scripts

#### 📄 `references\php-audit-bug-catalogue.md`

```markdown
# PHP Audit Bug Catalogue

Annotated recurring patterns observed in a real audit of a Persian invoice SaaS ("Factorchi", PHP 8, custom router, PDO, MySQL). Use as a pointing list when auditing similar billing/subscription apps. Format per entry: **Pattern** — code smell — symptom — fix.

## 1. Quota consumed by BOTH create and edit; edits blocked when quota exhausted
- Code: `InvoiceController::update()` ran `getQuotaStatus()` then `consumeQuota()` on every successful edit, and returned "buy a subscription" when `remaining <= 0`.
- Symptom: free plan (3/mo) users who hit the limit can no longer edit ANY invoice; each edit permanently burns one of the month's 3 slots; deleting invoices never refunds.
- Fix: consume only on create, or split create-quota from edit-quota; add a refund on delete; put the check+increment into one atomic `UPDATE ... SET quota_used = quota_used + 1 WHERE id = ? AND quota_used < ?`.

## 2. Check-then-act TOCTOU on quota and on coupon max_uses
- Pattern: `if (remaining > 0) { insert; increment }` across separate queries.
- Symptom: double-click / parallel submissions exceed the limit (two invoices on the last slot).
- Fix: single atomic UPDATE with `WHERE used < limit` and check `rowCount()`; wrap invoice+item insert in a transaction.

## 3. Persian/Arabic digits silently intval() to 0
- Pattern: Jalali→Gregorian helper doing `preg_split(...)` then `array_map('intval', $parts)` directly on user input; the admin form's placeholder literally shows Persian digits ("Persian/Persian/Persian").
- Symptom: `fromJalali('Persian/Persian/Persian')` returns NULL → paid subscription saved with `end_date = NULL` → `isActive()` (which requires non-empty end_date) returns false → the user paid but runs free-plan limits (PDF/Excel locked, 3-invoice quota) with no visible error.
- Fix: normalize Persian-Persian/Persian-Persian to ASCII before parsing; validate day ≤ days-in-month; test both digit sets.

## 3. Stale `status` column for subscriptions
- Pattern: `activatePlan()` sets `status='active'`; nothing flips it when `end_date < CURDATE()`.
- Symptom: `isPaidActive()` gates correctly by date, but admin UI renders the stored column → shows "Persian" (active) for expired plans; admin can't spot churn.
- Fix: compute `active = (status='active' AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= CURDATE()))` in a view/query alias; optionally a cron that flips status at expiry.

## 4. Coupon consumed at submission, not approval
- Pattern: `storePurchase()` increments `used_count` for the discount code at receipt-submission time.
- Symptom: a REJECTED payment permanently burns a `max_uses=1` coupon; also allows coupon hoarding races.
- Fix: `incrementUsage()` inside `approveReceipt()` only; `decrementUsage()` on rejection.

## 5. Invalid coupon silently dropped server-side
- Pattern: AJAX validates the code, but `storePurchase()` re-validates and, on failure, silently proceeds at full price while storing the discounted amount in the receipt row.
- Symptom: user believes a discount applied, admin later sees full-price receipt; revenue mismatch without any warning.
- Fix: error-out the form when the submitted code is present but invalid; store the code that was ACTUALLY applied.

## 6. Client-side gating for "premium" outputs
- Pattern: PDF/PNG generated purely in the browser (html2canvas + jsPDF); free users see a locked button, but browser Print equals the same output.
- Symptom: premium feature is free to anyone who prints.
- Fix: server-side generated PDF with a plan check, or drop PDF from the paid tier. Note the Excel endpoint was correctly server-side gated (`features['allow_excel']` check in the controller).

## 7. Deleting a parent plan cascades away history
- Pattern: `payment_receipts.plan_id REFERENCES plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, and `Plan::delete()` only migrates `subscriptions` to the free plan.
- Symptom: deleting a paid plan silently erases every receipt/payment audit row for it.
- Fix: FK `ON DELETE SET NULL` (receipt keeps plan_name via a LEFT JOIN lookup, or snapshot plan name on the row).

## 8. Feature/data lookups duplicated per page
- Pattern: controllers call `isPaidActive()` + `getPlanFeatures()` and the layout calls both AGAIN (`layouts/dashboard.php`) plus the view calls `(new Subscription())->getPlanFeatures()` a third time (subscription plans page).
- Symptom: 8-12 redundant queries per page; several trigger `getForUser()` inserts.
- Fix: per-request static cache keyed by method+userId in the Subscription model (e.g. `private static array $cache = []`).

## 9. Missing indexes on payment/status tables
- Pattern: `payment_receipts` has no index on `status` or `(user_id, status)`.
- Symptom: admin dashboard count + pending-list scans the whole table once receipts grow.
- Fix: add `INDEX (status)`, `INDEX (user_id, status)`.

## 10. Migration vs fresh-schema drift
- Pattern: `database/schema.sql` (v6) coexisted with `migration_v2..v6.sql`; the migrations use `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (MySQL 8.0.29+/MariaDB ONLY).
- Symptom: upgrade on MySQL 8.0.28 or older fails at the SLQ statement; fresh installs and upgrades diverge.
- Fix for audits: diff schema vs final migration columns explicitly and report drift; document min MySQL version.

## 11. Sub-folder router prefix stripping
- Pattern: Router strips `dirname(SCRIPT_NAME)` via plain `str_starts_with`, so `/invoice-app2/...` matches the prefix and corrupts the route.
- Symptom: sibling install directories sharing a prefix 404 or route oddly.
- Fix: compare with a boundary check (`$uri === $scriptDir || str_starts_with($uri, $scriptDir . '/')`).

## 12. Login-throttle keyed by email only
- Pattern: throttle key `'user:' . $email` in-session only.
- Symptom: attacker can lock out a target account by email rotation; throttling bypassable; acknowledged in code comments as a limitation.
- Fix: include IP; consider per-IP+email.

## 13. UTF-8 PHP files flagged "binary" by the file reader
- Pattern: `read_file` returned `Binary file - cannot display` for plain UTF-8 PHP with Persian comments (no BOM).
- Workaround (worked this session): `file models/User.php` showed "PHP script, UTF-8 text"; read with terminal `nl -ba`. Reported as a tooling pitfall, not an app bug.
```

### ⚙️ YAML Configuration (`SKILL.md` Frontmatter)

description: Audit PHP apps for SQLi, XSS, CSRF, IDOR, uploads, sessions.
name: php-security-audit
```

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# PHP Web-App Security Audit (Read-only)

Use when a PHP app (especially MVC-style: `index.php` front controller routing to `app/controllers/`, `app/models/`, `app/views/`) needs a security audit — SQLi, XSS, CSRF gaps, authz/IDOR, insecure uploads, brute-force, info disclosure. The audit is **read-only** — output is a findings report, never edits to audited code.

## Workflow (proven order — captures the most)

1. **Enumerate** the tree (`find . -type f -o -name '*.php'`) to map PHP files, `.htaccess` files, `uploads/` and `database/` dirs.
2. **Read `index.php` first** — it's the route table. List every endpoint; every POST route is a CSRF+authz target, every admin route an auth-check target.
3. **Read core framework** (`app/core/*.php`, config) to learn the security primitives the app *claims*:
   - DB layer: PDO prepared statements? `ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES=false`? parameterized `query()` helper?
   - Auth: regenerate id on login? CSRF token + `hash_equals`? lockout keyed by IP or by **session**?
   - Escaping helper `e()` / `htmlspecialchars` used consistently in views?
   - Config defaults: `APP_DEBUG` on? Committed secrets/credentials?
4. **Read every controller** (user + admin). For each method confirm: auth is at the top (`requireAdmin`/`requireSuperAdmin`/`requireUser`) — check per method, not per class — and that queries scope by session identity (`WHERE user_id = ?`) not just request id → IDOR.
5. **Read every model** hunting string-interpolated SQL: `%\$var` concatenation, `LIKE "%$x%"`, `ORDER BY $col`, `LIMIT $offset`, `DATE_ADD($base, ...)` (classic latent SQLi). Check raw TOCTOU races (quota/discount: validate-then-increment non-atomic).
6. **XSS via views**: grep output not wrapped in the escape helper, e.g.
   `grep -rn '<?=' --include='*.php' views/ | grep -vE 'e\(|\(int\)|csrfField|formatNumber|urlencode'`
   then triage hits; also grep raw `echo `, `innerHTML`/`document.write` in JS. **JSON sinks**: `grep -rn 'json_encode' --include='*.php' app/` — any `<?= json_encode($x)` inside a `<script>` block without `JSON_HEX_*` flags is a `</script>` breakout XSS when `$x` carries attacker-controlled strings (invoice item names, user fields). `JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE` does NOT escape `<`. This sink is invisible to the `<?=` grep above — run the json_encode grep in every app, not just when suspicious.
7. **Uploads**: MIME sniffed via finfo (content) vs extension-only (bad); filename random + extension derived from MIME map (good); size limit; upload-dir `.htaccess` blocking PHP execution (verify it covers subdirs); **SVG in the allowlist = stored XSS** (script runs on direct navigation; no CSP in headers = no mitigation).
8. **Auth flows**: `password_hash`/`password_verify`; reset token stored as **hash of token** vs plaintext; single-use + expiry; session fixation (`session_regenerate_id(true)`); logout via GET (CSRF-able).
9. **Non-code spots**: README.md + `database/schema.sql` often contain the **seed admin email + plaintext password** (CRITICAL). Check `.htaccess` (Indexes, FilesMatch rules, security headers) and `APP_DEBUG` default (error/DB-detail disclosure).
10. **Server-side price re-verification**: client-supplied plan/discount/amount must be re-resolved server-side from DB rows; client-trusted final prices are a pricing bug.

## Extended scope: bugs & structure audit

Use the same traversal when the ask is general (logic bugs, PHP 8.x compat, dead code, duplicates, broken routes), not just security:

11. **Route/link integrity**: extract registered routes from `index.php` (`grep -oE "\$router->(get|post)\('[^']+'"`), then extract every `href`/`action` literal / `APP_URL . '...'` fragment from all views + JS and check each base path resolves. Inline template literals like `APP_URL . '/invoices/view?id=' . (int)$inv['id']` won't match a naive grep — strip the `?id=` query part before comparing. Run `scripts/check_routes.py` (standalone, no deps) instead of hand-rolling.
12. **PHP 8.x compat scan**: `php -l` every file (XAMPP: `/c/xampp/php/php.exe -l`); grep for removed functions (`strftime|create_function|each|money_format|mysql_|FILTER_SANITIZE_STRING|ereg|split`), and implicit-nullable param deprecation (PHP 8.4+): `function\s+\w+\([^)]*?\w+\s+\$\w+\s*=\s*null` **without** a preceding `?` type. All these lint clean ≠ compatible; the deprecation regex catches what lint won't.
13. **Locale/date logic** (Persian/Jalali & similar): flag which calendar the *business logic* keys on vs the *UI*: e.g. monthly quota reset using `date('Y-m')` (Gregorian) in an app where users think in Jalali months. Validate Jahali conversion helpers: day-in-month bounds (Esfand can have 29 days in leap years; `fromJalali('1404/12/30')` silently rolls to `1405/01/01` instead of erroring). Free-text dates stored raw without round-tripping through the app's own converter = missing validation.
14. **Data-lifecycle / business logic**: FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` rows that delete real history when a parent is removed (deleting a plan wiping payment receipts). Duplicate checks that exist on CREATE but not UPDATE (unique email/code → uncaught PDOException/500 in update). TOCTOU quota/discount consume (check-then-increment non-atomic). Auto-computed dates that base on *today* instead of max(today, current end_date) when renewing/extending (admin helper pre-fill).
15. **Dead code & duplication** (structure audits): grep each public method for callsites (`grep -rn "methodName" --include='*.php' . | grep -v "function "`); flag copies of the same validation loop across controllers/models where one copy dropped a check (inconsistency is the bug, not the duplication).

## Report shape (the deliverable)

- Findings ordered by severity, each: **SEVERITY (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) — one-line title**
  - **file:line** — exact reference
  - **Bug** — observable attack / what's wrong
  - **Fix** — exact code change to apply
- End with a **top-10 prioritized remediation list**. Also list what is *correct* (prepared SQL everywhere, CSRF on all POSTs, per-user scoping) — proves real auditing, not pattern harvesting.

## Pitfalls

- **read_file flags UTF-8 PHP with Persian/Arabic text + U+200B ZWNJ as "binary"** → "Binary file" error. The file is valid; read it via `sed -n '1,400p' file.php` in the terminal (git-bash). `grep` also works on such files.
- Cite **file:line precisely** (fixes get verified by line); re-check content before citing.
- Brute-force lockouts **keyed by session are bypassable** (attacker drops cookies) — rate MEDIUM/HIGH; recommend an IP+email store with conditional UPDATE.
- Client-facing "price/discount/live-check" GET endpoints with no rate limit are payment-abuse vectors.
- Authz: check DELETE/UPDATE/EXPORT routes too, not only GET view routes.
- Don't claim "no session fixation" without testing every entry point (user login, admin login, password reset).
- The `search_files` tool mangles regex patterns containing parentheses (`query\(` becomes `query/(` and fails to compile) — for any pattern with parens/alternation, drop to terminal `grep -rn` (also needed anyway for UTF-8/ZWNJ files).
- Severity of JSON-in-`<script>` XSS depends on who can be tricked into opening the page: a `</script>` payload that lands in an admin-facing edit view is admin-account takeover (stored; attacker = any registered user); in a self-only edit view it's lower. Rate accordingly.
- Cost fix for the JSON sink is `json_encode($x, JSON_HEX_TAG|JSON_HEX_AMP|JSON_HEX_APOS|JSON_HEX_QUOT)` — and add `JSON_HEX_TAG` even when data looks safe; "UNESCAPED_UNICODE doesn't escape `<`" is the trap.
- Create-vs-update asymmetry: a unique-key check that exists in `store()` but is missing in `update()` (same form, duplicate email/code) ends in an uncaught PDOException → ugly 500; check both paths and exclude self (`email != current`).
- SQL `ON DELETE CASCADE` on history tables: deleting the parent (plan/product/category) silently deletes billing/payment history. Prefer `SET NULL` + snapshot column (denormalized plan name) for money/audit tables.
- Locale audits: checkout whether *business* counters (quota resets, periods) use the same calendar as the *UI*; Persian apps keying quota on `date('Y-m')` reset mid-Jalali-month.
- `read_file` misreads UTF-8 Persian PHP files — that pitfall plus grep-paren mangling above apply to the entire audit, not just security passes.

See `references/audit-example-invoice-app.md` for a worked security example (Persian PHP invoice app — findings included seeded super-admin credentials published in README/schema, reset-link disclosure under `APP_DEBUG=true`, session-keyed lockout bypass, SVG stored-XSS upload, plaintext reset tokens, JSON-in-`<script>` breakout XSS; the "correct" list also shows what to verify as safe).

See `references/bugs-structure-checklists.md` for the AUDIT-2 extension: PHP 8.x compat grep set, Jalali-date bound checks, route-verification approach, dead-code/duplication greps, and the concrete finding set from the same app (JSON tag-break XSS, plan-delete cascading receipts, quota TOCTOU, Gregorian-vs-Jalali quota key, implicit `allow_*` features). Run `scripts/check_routes.py` (standalone, stdlib-only) to verify href/action literals against index.php route registrations.


### 📚 Auxiliary References, Templates & Scripts

#### 📄 `references\audit-example-invoice-app.md`

```markdown
# Worked example — Persian PHP invoice app ("Factorchi") audit

Read-only audit of `<USER_HOME>/Downloads/invoice-app` (MVC: `index.php` router, `app/controllers/`, `app/controllers/admin/`, `app/models/`, `app/core/`, `app/views/`). Findings below demonstrate the severity/file:line/description/fix shape.

## Findings (top of the final list)

1. **CRITICAL — Seed super-admin credentials published in the repo.** `README.md:31-33` lists live admin email + plaintext password; `database/schema.sql:195-199` seeds that account as `super_admin`. Anyone with the repo (or a deployed site's README) has the admin password. Fix: random password generated at install; force change on first login; remove creds from README/schema.
2. **CRITICAL — Password-reset link disclosed → account takeover.** `app/config/config.php:40` ships `APP_DEBUG=true`; `app/controllers/AuthController.php:173-176` flashes the working reset URL into the session; `app/views/auth/forgot-password.php:12-16` prints it. Attacker knowing a victim's email gets a live reset link → full user account takeover. Fix: only render the debug link when request is from loopback (`REMOTE_ADDR` in 127.0.0.1/::1) AND debug; default APP_DEBUG=false.
3. **HIGH — Brute-force lockout keyed by session, trivially bypassed.** `app/core/Auth.php:129-166` stores attempts in `$_SESSION['login_attempts']`; attacker rotates/drops cookies → unlimited tries on `/login` and `/admin/login`. Fix: IP+email keyed attempts in DB with conditional UPDATE, backoff, CAPTCHA.
4. **MEDIUM — Stored XSS via SVG logo/favicon upload.** `app/controllers/admin/AdminSettingsController.php:41,84-118` allows `image/svg+xml` with no sanitization; SVG scripts run when `uploads/branding/<name>.svg` is opened directly (no CSP). Fix: drop SVG from allowlist or sanitize strictly; add CSP.
5. **MEDIUM — Reset tokens stored plaintext in DB.** `app/models/User.php:97-111` stores/compares the raw 64-hex token. DB leak → live reset tokens. Fix: store `hash('sha256', token)` and query by hash; keep single-use invalidation.
6. **MEDIUM — Email enumeration via register.** `app/controllers/AuthController.php:42-44` "email already registered" message; unthrottled `/register` (mass account spam). Fix: generic message + per-IP limits.
7. **MEDIUM — No rate limits on payment-adjacent endpoints.** `/subscription/check-discount` (index.php:74), `/admin/users/calc-end-date` (index.php:88). Fix: per-IP throttle middleware.
8. **LOW — Latent SQLi (not currently reachable).** `app/models/Subscription.php:205-216` interpolates `$base = "'".$current['end_date']."'"` into `DATE_ADD($base, INTERVAL $months MONTH)`. Currently safe because end_date only written via strict `fromJalali()` — still flag + fix with format validation and bound params.
9. **LOW — Error/DB detail disclosure.** `app/core/Database.php:26-28` dies with the PDO exception message under APP_DEBUG.
10. **LOW — GET logout CSRF** (`index.php:44,79`), **missing CSP**, **admin email uniqueness not checked** (`AdminUserController::updateInfo` → `User::adminUpdate`), **TOCTOU races** on quota (`User::consumeQuota`) and discount usage (`DiscountCode::validateCode` + `incrementUsage`).
11. **HIGH (2nd pass) — Stored XSS via `json_encode()` inside `<script>` (JSON-in-script breakout).** `app/views/invoices/create.php:122` and `app/views/admin/invoices/edit.php:43` emit `<?= json_encode($items, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE) ?>` in a `<script type="application/json">` block. A product name like `</script><script>...</script>` (fully attacker-controlled via `invoice_items.product_name`) terminates the script block → raw HTML injection. Only the invoice owner edits via `create.php`, BUT any user can plant the payload and then any admin opening `/admin/invoices/edit?id=N` executes it in the admin origin → create-admin / settings tampering (chain to full admin takeover). The standard `<?=`-without-`e()` grep misses it entirely because the sink is inside a script block — detection requires `grep -rn 'json_encode' app/views/`. Fix: `json_encode($items, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_HEX_TAG | JSON_HEX_AMP | JSON_HEX_APOS | JSON_HEX_QUOT)` (or render via DOM text node).

## Verified-correct list (report these too)

- All queries parameterized via PDO (`Database::query`, `ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES=false`); only string SQL was the LOW #8.
- Every state-changing POST route calls `verifyCsrfOrDie()`; every form emits `Auth::csrfField()` (spot-checked views incl. admin forms).
- All admin methods gate on `Auth::requireAdmin()`/`requireSuperAdmin()` per method; user routes scope by `user_id` (`Invoice::findForUser`, receipts by session user) — no IDOR found.
- Uploads (raster): finfo MIME allowlist, size caps, random hex names, extension from MIME map, `uploads/.htaccess` blocks execution; `app/` and `database/` denied.
- `session_regenerate_id(true)` on login/logout; HttpOnly+Lax cookies; bcrypt `password_hash`; `e()` escaping used in all views (reflected search/flash escaped).

## Tactical notes from the session

- `read_file` refused UTF-8 PHP with Persian comments + ZWNJ bytes ("Binary file") — read via `sed -n '1,Np'` in terminal; `grep` unaffected.
- Route inventory came from `index.php` (all GET/POST listed) before touching controllers — it determined the full attack surface.
- Views XSS sweep: one grep command filtered everything except ~6 safe hits (numeric/static template data) — fast triage. **Second sweep required**: `grep -rn 'json_encode' app/views/` — this found the HIGH #11 sink the `<?=` grep never sees.
- Default-credential check (README + schema.sql grep for email/password) yielded the top finding; do it early.
```

#### 📄 `references\bugs-structure-checklists.md`

```markdown
# PHP App — Bugs & Structure Audit Checklists (AUDIT-2 extension)

Companion to `audit-example-invoice-app.md`. Same class of work (read-only audit of an MVC-index.php PHP app), focusing on **logic bugs, PHP 8.x compat, dead/duplicated code, date/locale issues, quota/subscription math, broken routes, performance**. Worked example: «Factorchi» Persian invoice SaaS (app/controllers|models|core|views, index.php route table).

## Reusable scans

```bash
# 1. PHP lint on every file (XAMPP CLI)
for f in $(find . -name "*.php"); do /c/xampp/php/php.exe -l "$f" 2>&1 | grep -v "No syntax errors"; done

# 2. PHP 8.x removed/deprecated functions
grep -rnE '\b(strftime|create_function|each|money_format|mysql_|ereg|split|FILTER_SANITIZE_STRING)\s*\(' --include='*.php' .

# 3. PHP 8.4 implicit-nullable deprecation (param typed WITHOUT '?' but default null)
grep -rnE 'function\s+\w+\([^)]*(?<![\?])\b\w+\s+\$\w+\s*=\s*null' --include='*.php' .   # see caveat: search_files mangles parens — use terminal grep

# 4. JSON sink inside <script> (XSS breakout)
grep -rn 'json_encode(' --include='*.php' app/ views/

# 5. Dead code: method with no callers besides its own definition
grep -rn 'methodName' --include='*.php' . | grep -v 'function methodName'

# 6. Built-up route literals (APP_URL . '...' concatenation) — see scripts/check_routes.py
```

## Finding set from this app (worked examples, keep as patterns)

- **`</script>` breakout via JSON**: `<script type="application/json"><?= json_encode($items, JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE) ?></script>` — `json_encode` doesn't escape `<`/`>`; product_name = `</script><script>alert(1)</script>` breaks the tag. Executes in any editor of that invoice — incl. admin editing a user's invoice (admin-account XSS). Fix: `JSON_HEX_TAG|JSON_HEX_AMP|JSON_HEX_APOS|JSON_HEX_QUOT` or escape server-side into HTML-escaped cells. Also `String(name).replace(/"/g,'&quot;')` in innerHTML is NOT enough (only quote-escapes; backtick in a JS template-literal injects a syntax error, `<>` attribute values are benign — but don't rely on it).
- **Cascade history loss**: `payment_receipts.plan_id → plans(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` + a `plan delete` that only remaps subscriptions = approved receipt history silently wiped. Prefer `SET NULL` + snapshot plan name on the receipt row at creation.
- **Create/update asymmetry**: register/store validates duplicate email/code; update paths skip it → unique-key PDOException → uncaught 500 (display_errors on). Check both and exclude self.
- **Quota/limit TOCTOU**: `getQuotaStatus()` (check remaining) then separate `UPDATE users SET quota_used = quota_used+1` (no `WHERE remaining>0` guard) → N concurrent requests over-consume. Atomic: `UPDATE ... SET quota_used=quota_used+1 WHERE id=? AND quota_used < ?` + examine rowCount.
- **Consume-on-edit policy**: each save of an existing invoice burns a unit; delete never refunds; user with remaining=0 can't even edit. Big UX/product trap — flag the policy decision, not just the code.
- **Locale mismatch**: quota month keyed `date('Y-m')` (Gregorian) in a Persian-Jalali app → resets mid-Jalali-month, unpredictable to users. Key on the Jalali `Y/m` (substr of todayJalali()).
- **Jalali converter bound-check**: only jm 1..12 / jd 1..31 checked; June-rollover: `1404/12/30` (Esfand=29 days) silently becomes `1405/01/01`. Also free-text invoice date never validated (would be via toJalali/fromJalali round-trip).
- **Renewal date math**: admin auto-fill computed month-end from *today* — discards remaining days. Correct: base = max(today, current end_date) when the current sub is unexpired.
- **Per-request query duplication**: `getPlanFeatures()` calls `getForUser()` then `isPaidActive()` calls `getForUser()` again (and the layout calls isPaidActive + daysLeft) → same 30-column JOIN 3–6×/request. Memoize per request. Relational COUNT subquery per row in admin list OK at 20 rows.
- **SVG upload** = stored XSS on direct URL open if no CSP (even with upload-dir PHP execution blocked); drop SVG from allowlist or serve with nosniff + inline disposition.
- **Route check**: all literals resolved in this app; the routine still pays off (query strings must be stripped before comparing base paths).

## Report conventions that worked
- Section the report: CRITICAL (XSS, data loss) · HIGH (logic/authz gaps) · MEDIUM (date/quota semantics) · PERFORMANCE · DEAD CODE/DUPLICATION · PHP-8 COMPAT · RTL/DATE · ROUTE CHECK · ERROR-HANDLING.
- State what PASSED (lint clean, no removed functions, all routes resolve) — brevity, not just a scare list.
- Write the report file to the cache path the parent passed (e.g. `C:/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/hermes/cache/t/audit_bugs.md`); print a ≤6-line stdout summary with severity, file:line, impact, will-fix.
```

#### 📄 `references\json-file-backend-audit.md`

```markdown
# JSON-file Backend Audit — worked checklist (React+Vite portfolio + PHP JSON store)

From a full-project audit of a Vite+React 19 portfolio (Tailwind 4, react-router 7) with a PHP
JSON-file admin backend under `public/api/` (shared `_lib.php`, data files under
`public/api/admin/data/`, pre-built demo sub-projects under `public/Projects/`).

## CRITICAL

1. **Default admin credentials fallback (config file missing → admin/admin123).**
   `get_admin_config()` returned a hardcoded `username=admin`, `password_sha256=sha256("admin123")`
   (`240be518...`), and a fixed HMAC `secret` whenever `data/config.json` was absent.
   `git status` showed `D public/api/admin/data/config.json` — deleted from the working tree AND
   tracked history, so the fallback was live. Anyone knowing the source (it's public on GitHub)
   can log in.
   Fix: ship a real config.json with a random secret, or fail closed (no config file → 503),
   never fall back to known-good defaults. Also use `password_hash`/`password_verify` (bcrypt)
   instead of raw sha256 — sha256 is a fast brute-force target.

2. **Dev mock-fetch fallback ships in the production bundle.**
   `useAdminAuth.jsx` wrapped every call (`login`, `authFetch`, `check`) in `try { real fetch }
   catch { mockFetch }` where `mockFetch` accepted hardcoded `admin`/`admin123` and returned a
   demo DB (fake stats, fake messages, fake clicks). Confirmed present in the built output:
   `grep -o "admin123\|admin_mock_db\|mockFetch" dist/assets/index-*.js` hits.
   Consequences: (a) real API error/network failure → login succeeds with demo creds;
   (b) expired token → `authFetch` gets 401 → catch → mock returns fake data, panel NEVER logs
   out; (c) `auth-check` failure → mock returns `{ok:true}` → `valid=true`.
   Fix: gate mock behind `import.meta.env.DEV` (or a Vite dev-only plugin — the project already
   had `vite-plugin-mock-api.js` wired via `configureServer`, which is the CORRECT pattern);
   never fall back to mock in production; on 401 call `logout()`.

## HIGH

3. **CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on admin endpoints.** Shared `_lib.php` headers set
   `*` + `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization` for every `/api/admin/*`
   route. Any origin can replay a stolen bearer token and read responses.
   Fix: restrict to same-origin / explicit host list; public endpoints can stay `*`.

4. **No rate limiting anywhere.** `auth.php` brute-forceable (and fast sha256), public
   `messages.php` POST unlimited (spam + unbounded JSON growth), `track.php`/`track-click.php`
   public (visit/click stats forgeable by bots).
   Fix: per-IP throttles on auth, length caps + honeypot/CAPTCHA on contact, rate limit on track.

## MEDIUM

5. **Real visitor data in git.** `public/api/admin/data/messages.json` (names, phone numbers),
   `visits.json`, `online.json` (session ids) show as `M` in `git status` — committing them leaks
   visitor PII into a public repo. Fix: gitignore the data dir (keep `.gitkeep` + deny
   `.htaccess`).

6. **Dead broken endpoint.** `project.php` filters projects on `$p["slug"]` but `projects.json`
   entries have no `slug` field → always 404. Unused by the frontend but a latent trap if wired
   up later. Flag during route/link integrity checks.

7. **Broken links as real bugs.** `href="#"` placeholders: Footer LinkedIn, Instagram in both
   ContactBox and SubjectBox. For design audits of this site, grep `href="#"` — they read as
   dead UI, not TODOs.

8. **Layout overflow.** Home page `gap-10 lg:gap-96` (384px) between text and music card exceeds
   1024–1200px viewport widths; `body { overflow-x: hidden }` silently clips content. Check
   large-gap layouts at the lg breakpoint before calling them "airy design".

## Verified correct (don't re-flag)

- Token: HMAC-sha256 signed, `exp` checked, `hash_equals` for signature comparison.
- `write_json_file`: `fopen("c")` + `flock(LOCK_EX)` + truncate (the READ path lacks a lock —
  that's finding (f), but the write side is right).
- `public/api/admin/data/.htaccess` denies direct HTTP access.
- Frontend click tracking throttled 500ms per key; abort controller on route change.

## Audit quick-commands

```bash
git status -s public/api/admin/data/          # committed visitor data / deleted config
grep -o "admin123\|admin_mock_db\|mockFetch" dist/assets/index-*.js   # mock in prod bundle
grep -rn "href=\"#\"" src/ --include="*.jsx"  # dead links
for f in $(find public/api -name "*.php"); do php -l "$f"; done      # syntax sweep
```
```

#### 📄 `references\jsonstore-fix-techniques.md`

```markdown
# Fix techniques for the JSON-file backend class (proven in a live remediation)

Companion to `json-file-backend-audit.md` / `portfolio-jsonstore-audit.md` (which list the
FINDINGS). This file records the FIX TECHNIQUES that worked, for the same class of app:
React+Vite SPA + PHP admin API persisting to JSON files under `public/api/admin/data/`.

## 1. Soft vs hard rate limits — pick per endpoint

- **Hard (fail-closed)**: login, contact-form. 5 failed attempts per IP → 15-min lockout,
  plus `usleep(250000)` on failure to slow brute force. Returns 429.
- **Soft (silently drop)**: high-frequency public endpoints — visit tracker and 25s
  heartbeats. A real visitor's heartbeat bursts would trip a hard limit and 429 them.
  Budget e.g. 120 req/60s per IP; once exceeded, return `{"ok":true}` pretend-success
  WITHOUT writing anything. This keeps stats honest for humans and useless for spam bots.
- Implementation: shared `_lib.php` helpers `rate_check()` (hard) + `rate_check_soft()`
  (soft), both keyed by `client_ip()` (respect `HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR` first entry),
  persisted in a `rate.json` with periodic pruning of expired windows.

## 2. Token revocation without a session store

Stateless JSON backend → logout can't invalidate tokens by deleting a session. Fix:
- `issue_token()` adds `"ver" => (int)$config["token_version"]` to the HMAC payload.
- `verify_token()` rejects any token whose `ver` ≠ current `config["token_version"]`.
- Bumping `token_version` in config.json invalidates every outstanding token at once.
Costs one integer field; gives real server-side logout/revoke on a sessionless store.

## 3. Lock the READ path, not just the write

Writes commonly use `fopen($path,"c") + flock(LOCK_EX) + ftruncate + rewind` — but the
READ side via bare `file_get_contents` races that: it can read a half-written/truncated
file → `json_decode` returns null → default → lost data under concurrent track hits.
Fix: `fopen($path,"r") + flock(LOCK_SH) + stream_get_contents + flock(LOCK_UN) + fclose`.
Do this in the shared `read_json_file()` so every caller inherits it.

## 4. Config fail-closed, never known-default fallback

`get_admin_config()` returning a hardcoded `admin`/`sha256("admin123")`/fixed secret
when config.json is missing = backdoor. Fix:
- Missing config → return `username=""`, `password_sha256=""`,
  `secret=bin2hex(random_bytes(32))` — login impossible, tokens un-forgeable,
  and the secret changes per request so nothing is stable to attack.
- Restore the real config.json from git (`git checkout -- <path>`).
- Remove the same hardcoded default from the dev mock layer (`vite-plugin-mock-api.js`).

## 5. Verify DEV-gating in the BUILT bundle (not just source)

`import.meta.env.DEV` gating in source is NOT proof it works — Vite statically replaces
it, and minifiers rename things. After building, verify:
```bash
grep -c "import.meta.env" dist/assets/index-*.js      # expect 0 (fully inlined)
grep -c "admin123" dist/assets/index-*.js             # expect 0 (mock cred gone)
grep -o "admin_mock_db\|mockFetch" dist/assets/index-*.js | sort | uniq -c
```
If `admin123`/`_mock_db` still appears, the fallback is LIVE in production regardless
of the source fix. In the verified case: `!import.meta.env.DEV` compiled to a constant
`true` in prod so the mock branch became dead code, but the mock strings remained until
the credential literals were also removed from the mock DB factory.

## 6. CORS: same-origin for authenticated endpoints

Shared `_lib.php` headers used `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` + `Allow-Headers:
Content-Type, Authorization` → any origin could replay a stolen bearer token.
Fix: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <echo HTTP_ORIGIN or "null">` + `Vary: Origin` +
`Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: false`. Public GET endpoints may stay open.

## 7. Git hygiene for live data

- `git rm --cached public/api/admin/data/*.json` and add to `.gitignore`
  (keep `config.json` tracked if it holds the real credentials — or gitignore it too and
  commit `config.example.json`; user preference varies).
- Check `git status -s public/api/admin/data/` during audits — Modified JSON files there
  mean live visitor PII (names, phones, session ids) is staged to be committed.
```

#### 📄 `references\portfolio-jsonstore-audit.md`

```markdown
# React SPA + PHP/JSON-store Portfolio — Audit Pattern

Architecture (my-portfolio-site-react, recurring in this user's portfolio work):
- Vite/React SPA. Public pages fetch `/api/*.json` (static) or `/api/*.php`.
- Admin panel (React, route `/admin/*`) talks to `/api/admin/*.php`, which read/write
  JSON files in `public/api/admin/data/` (config.json, visits.json, messages.json,
  online.json, clicks.json).
- Auth = Bearer token (HMAC-signed base64url payload `{u, exp}` + signature, 7-day TTL),
  stored in localStorage. No CSRF tokens, no server sessions.

## Findings that recur in this class (all observed in a real audit)

### 1. Missing/deleted config.json → DEFAULT admin credentials active
Config loader returns a hardcoded fallback: username `admin`, password = sha256("admin123"),
fixed HMAC secret. If `config.json` was deleted from git (`git status` shows
`D public/api/admin/data/config.json`), the fallback IS the live config → anyone logs in.
- AUDIT: read the config loader, inspect fallback defaults, `git status -s` on the data dir.
- FIX: refuse to run with defaults (write a real config on first boot), force password change,
  or fail closed when config.json is absent.

### 2. Mock API fallback shipped to PRODUCTION = auth bypass + fake data
Admin hook pattern: `try { fetch(realApi) } catch { mockFetch(url) }`. The in-browser mock
accepts the hardcoded admin/admin123 and returns fabricated stats/messages from localStorage.
Consequences in production:
- Backend error / network fail during login → mock accepts admin/admin123 → bypass.
- Expired token → real API returns 401 → authFetch's catch falls back to mock → mock
  returns 200 fake data → admin never logs out, sees fabricated numbers.
- auth-check fallback returns `{ok:true}` → `valid=true` on ANY backend failure.
- AUDIT: grep `mockFetch|catch .*mock|fallback` in admin hooks; trace 401 handling —
  an expired token MUST trigger logout, never fall through to mock.
- FIX: gate the mock behind `import.meta.env.DEV` only; on 401 → logout(); never fall back
  on failure.

### 3. CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on admin endpoints
Shared helper sets `*` plus `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization` on
every `/api/admin/*` endpoint → any origin can replay a stolen Bearer token.
- FIX: same-origin only (drop the header or echo the request origin + Vary: Origin).

### 4. Public POST endpoints with no rate limit / no length cap
Contact-form POST, track.php (visits), track-click.php run unauthenticated, no server-side
throttle (client-side ~500ms throttle is trivially bypassed), no max body length →
spam + unbounded JSON-file growth (disk-fill DoS) + forgeable analytics.
- AUDIT: enumerate POST endpoints that never call `require_auth()`; check length limits and
  throttling.
- FIX: length caps + per-IP rate limiting on write endpoints; consider CAPTCHA on contact.

### 5. Real visitor data staged in git
visits.json / messages.json / online.json hold real traffic and show as
Modified/untracked in `git status` → leaks visitor info if committed.
- AUDIT: `git status -s public/api/admin/data/`.
- FIX: .gitignore the data dir; commit a config.example.json template instead.

### 6. Dead endpoint filtering on a non-existent field
`project.php?slug=X` filters `$p["slug"]`, but projects.json records have no `slug` field →
always 404. Unused by the SPA (dead code), still a correctness bug.
- AUDIT: for every API filter predicate, verify the field actually exists in the JSON records.

### 7. PHP version gate undeclared
`str_contains`, arrow fns, `fn()` shorthand require PHP 8.0+; README declares no minimum →
white screen on PHP 7.x shared hosts.
- AUDIT: grep PHP-8-only functions; check README for a stated min version.

## Things that were CORRECT (verify, then don't flag)
- JSON writes use flock(LOCK_EX) — good (reads are unlocked → minor TOCTOU on concurrent
  track hits, LOW).
- `hash_equals` for username+password compare — good, but sha256 is a fast hash → pair with
  rate limiting (finding #4).
- Token signature verified with `hash_equals` + `exp` check — good.
- `data/.htaccess` denies direct HTTP access to the JSON data files — good.
```

#### 📄 `scripts\check_routes.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
check_routes.py — verify every route literal in a PHP MVC app resolves to a
registered route. Extracts registrations from index.php (`$router->get/post('...')`)
and every href/action literal (bare '/path' or APP_URL-concatenated) from views+JS,
strips query strings / PHP-snippet noise, and reports base paths with no route.

Usage:
    python check_routes.py [app_root] [index.php]

Assumes the classic shape: index.php with `$router->get('...', handler)` /
`$router->post('...', handler)` and views containing `APP_URL . '/xref'` or
`href="APP_URL ?>/path..."` literals. Stdlib only, Windows/git-bash safe.
"""
import os
import re
import sys


def find_routes(index_path):
    """Return set of base paths registered in index.php."""
    src = open(index_path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    routes = set(re.findall(r"\$router->(?:get|post)\('([^']+)'", src))
    return {r.split('?')[0].rstrip('/') or '/' for r in routes}


def collect_literals(root):
    """Yield candidate path strings from *.php views/layouts and assets/js."""
    pat = re.compile(r"(?:APP_URL\s*\.\s*)?'((?:/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)+(?:\?[^']*)?)'")
    refs = set()
    for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
        # skip vendor/database dumps to keep noise down
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in ('vendor', 'node_modules', 'database')]
        for fn in files:
            if fn.endswith('.php') or fn.endswith('.js'):
                txt = open(os.path.join(dirpath, fn), encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
                for m in pat.finditer(txt):
                    refs.add(m.group(1))
    return refs


def main():
    root = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else '.'
    index = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else os.path.join(root, 'index.php')
    if not os.path.isfile(index):
        print(f"index.php not found: {index}"); return 1

    routes = find_routes(index)
    refs = collect_literals(root)

    ignored_prefixes = ('/uploads', '/assets', '/css', '/js', '/fonts')
    broken = []
    for r in sorted(refs):
        base = r.split('?')[0].rstrip('/') or '/'
        if base in routes or base == '/':
            continue
        if base.startswith(ignored_prefixes) or base in ('/app', '/branding', '/samples'):
            continue  # static/asset path fragments, e.g. APP_URL . '/uploads/branding/'
        broken.append((r, base))

    print(f"index.php routes registered : {len(routes)}")
    print(f"literals found in views/js  : {len(refs)}")
    if broken:
        print(f"\nUNRESOLVED ({len(broken)}):")
        for lit, base in broken:
            print(f"  {lit}  -> base '{base}' has no route")
        return 1
    print("\nAll referenced paths resolve to a registered route.")
    return 0


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
```

    - design
    - documentation
name: plan
platforms:
- linux
- macos
- windows
version: 2.0.0
```

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# Plan Mode

Use this skill when the user wants a plan instead of execution.

## Core behavior

For this turn, you are planning only.

- Do not implement code.
- Do not edit project files except the plan markdown file.
- Do not run mutating terminal commands, commit, push, or perform external actions.
- You may inspect the repo or other context with read-only commands/tools when needed.
- Your deliverable is a markdown plan saved inside the active workspace under `.hermes/plans/`.

## Output requirements

Write a markdown plan that is concrete and actionable.

Include, when relevant:
- Goal
- Current context / assumptions
- Proposed approach
- Step-by-step plan
- Files likely to change
- Tests / validation
- Risks, tradeoffs, and open questions

If the task is code-related, include exact file paths, likely test targets, and verification steps.

## Save location

Save the plan with `write_file` under:
- `.hermes/plans/YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS-<slug>.md`

Treat that as relative to the active working directory / backend workspace. Hermes file tools are backend-aware, so using this relative path keeps the plan with the workspace on local, docker, ssh, modal, and daytona backends.

If the runtime provides a specific target path, use that exact path.
If not, create a sensible timestamped filename yourself under `.hermes/plans/`.

## Interaction style

- If the request is clear enough, write the plan directly.
- If no explicit instruction accompanies `/plan`, infer the task from the current conversation context.
- If it is genuinely underspecified, ask a brief clarifying question instead of guessing.
- After saving the plan, reply briefly with what you planned and the saved path.

---

# Writing the Plan Well

The rest of this skill is the craft of authoring a *good* implementation plan — the content that goes inside the markdown file above.

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the implementer has zero context for the codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need: which files to touch, complete code, testing commands, docs to check, how to verify. Give them bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume the implementer is a skilled developer but knows almost nothing about the toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Core principle:** A good plan makes implementation obvious. If someone has to guess, the plan is incomplete.

## When a Full Implementation Plan Helps

**Always use before:**
- Implementing multi-step features
- Breaking down complex requirements
- Delegating to subagents via subagent-driven-development

**Don't skip when:**
- Feature seems simple (assumptions cause bugs)
- You plan to implement it yourself (future you needs guidance)
- Working alone (documentation matters)

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each task = 2-5 minutes of focused work.**

Every step is one action:
- "Write the failing test" — step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" — step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" — step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" — step
- "Commit" — step

**Too big:**
```markdown
### Task 1: Build authentication system
[50 lines of code across 5 files]
```

**Right size:**
```markdown
### Task 1: Create User model with email field
[10 lines, 1 file]

### Task 2: Add password hash field to User
[8 lines, 1 file]

### Task 3: Create password hashing utility
[15 lines, 1 file]
```

## Plan Document Structure

### Header (Required)

Every plan MUST start with:

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For Hermes:** Use subagent-driven-development skill to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

### Task Structure

Each task follows this format:

````markdown
### Task N: [Descriptive Name]

**Objective:** What this task accomplishes (one sentence)

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/new_file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:45-67` (line numbers if known)
- Test: `tests/path/to/test_file.py`

**Step 1: Write failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

**Step 2: Run test to verify failure**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_specific_behavior -v`
Expected: FAIL — "function not defined"

**Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

**Step 4: Run test to verify pass**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_specific_behavior -v`
Expected: PASS

**Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## Writing Process

### Step 1: Understand Requirements

Read and understand:
- Feature requirements
- Design documents or user description
- Acceptance criteria
- Constraints

### Step 2: Explore the Codebase

Use Hermes tools to understand the project:

```python
# Understand project structure
search_files("*.py", target="files", path="src/")

# Look at similar features
search_files("similar_pattern", path="src/", file_glob="*.py")

# Check existing tests
search_files("*.py", target="files", path="tests/")

# Read key files
read_file("src/app.py")
```

### Step 3: Design Approach

Decide:
- Architecture pattern
- File organization
- Dependencies needed
- Testing strategy

### Step 4: Write Tasks

Create tasks in order:
1. Setup/infrastructure
2. Core functionality (TDD for each)
3. Edge cases
4. Integration
5. Cleanup/documentation

### Step 5: Add Complete Details

For each task, include:
- **Exact file paths** (not "the config file" but `src/config/settings.py`)
- **Complete code examples** (not "add validation" but the actual code)
- **Exact commands** with expected output
- **Verification steps** that prove the task works

### Step 6: Review the Plan

Check:
- [ ] Tasks are sequential and logical
- [ ] Each task is bite-sized (2-5 min)
- [ ] File paths are exact
- [ ] Code examples are complete (copy-pasteable)
- [ ] Commands are exact with expected output
- [ ] No missing context
- [ ] DRY, YAGNI, TDD principles applied

## Principles

### DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself)

**Bad:** Copy-paste validation in 3 places
**Good:** Extract validation function, use everywhere

### YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It)

**Bad:** Add "flexibility" for future requirements
**Good:** Implement only what's needed now

```python
# Bad — YAGNI violation
class User:
    def __init__(self, name, email):
        self.name = name
        self.email = email
        self.preferences = {}  # Not needed yet!
        self.metadata = {}     # Not needed yet!

# Good — YAGNI
class User:
    def __init__(self, name, email):
        self.name = name
        self.email = email
```

### TDD (Test-Driven Development)

Every task that produces code should include the full TDD cycle:
1. Write failing test
2. Run to verify failure
3. Write minimal code
4. Run to verify pass

See `test-driven-development` skill for details.

### Frequent Commits

Commit after every task:
```bash
git add [files]
git commit -m "type: description"
```

## Common Mistakes

### Vague Tasks

**Bad:** "Add authentication"
**Good:** "Create User model with email and password_hash fields"

### Incomplete Code

**Bad:** "Step 1: Add validation function"
**Good:** "Step 1: Add validation function" followed by the complete function code

### Missing Verification

**Bad:** "Step 3: Test it works"
**Good:** "Step 3: Run `pytest tests/test_auth.py -v`, expected: 3 passed"

### Missing File Paths

**Bad:** "Create the model file"
**Good:** "Create: `src/models/user.py`"

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer the execution approach:

**"Plan complete and saved. Ready to execute using subagent-driven-development — I'll dispatch a fresh subagent per task with two-stage review (spec compliance then code quality). Shall I proceed?"**

When executing, use the `subagent-driven-development` skill:
- Fresh `delegate_task` per task with full context
- Spec compliance review after each task
- Code quality review after spec passes
- Proceed only when both reviews approve

## Remember

```
Bite-sized tasks (2-5 min each)
Exact file paths
Complete code (copy-pasteable)
Exact commands with expected output
Verification steps
DRY, YAGNI, TDD
Frequent commits
```

**A good plan makes implementation obvious.**

#### 📄 `scripts\amoot-account-check.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Probe Amoot account health: token validity + web-service activation.
# Reads AMOOT_TOKEN from the project's .env and calls AccountStatus.
# Status "User_WebServiceBanned" => web service not enabled on the account (panel-side fix).
set -euo pipefail

REPO="${1:-<USER_HOME>/Documents/GitHub/porskad}"
ENV_FILE="$REPO/.env"

if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: .env not found at $ENV_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

TOKEN="$(grep -E '^AMOOT_TOKEN=' "$ENV_FILE" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\r')"
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: AMOOT_TOKEN missing in $ENV_FILE" >&2
  exit 1
fi

echo "== Amoot AccountStatus =="
curl -s -X POST "https://portal.amootsms.com/rest/AccountStatus" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "Token=$TOKEN"
echo
echo "== Note: Status 'User_WebServiceBanned' = web service not activated in the Amoot panel =="
```

## SEO, AEO & GEO Infrastructure (Standing Rules)
- **OPEN GRAPH & SOCIAL CRAWLERS REQUIRE ABSOLUTE IMAGE URLS**: Telegram, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Twitter/X crawlers NEVER resolve relative image URLs like `/og-preview.png` and silently fail to render rich link preview cards. Always provide `https://<USER>-mehdi-sadeghi.vercel.app/og-preview.png` for `og:image`, `og:image:secure_url`, and `twitter:image`.
- **OpenGraph & Twitter Card Anatomy**: `og:type` (`website` / `article`), `og:site_name`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:url`, `og:image:width: 1200`, `og:image:height: 630`, `og:image:alt`, `og:locale: en_US`, `twitter:card: summary_large_image`.
- **Dynamic Per-Route Metadata (`usePageSEO`)**: Every route (`/`, `/project`, `/blog`, `/blog/:slug`, `/about`, `/contact`) manages its title, meta description, canonical link, and dynamic Schema.org JSON-LD structured data.
- **AEO (Answer Engine Optimization)**: Provide clear, direct-answer FAQPage schemas (`@type: FAQPage`) answering common entity queries (e.g. "Who is <USER> Mehdi Sadeghi?", "What technologies does he use?", "What projects has he built?", "How to contact him?").
- **GEO (Generative Engine Optimization)**: Maintain `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` at public root for LLM crawlers (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity) detailing the developer entity, verified skill stack, project directory, and technical publications.

## Admin Panel, Telegram & Durable Storage Laws
- **TOKEN SECRET INITIALIZATION IN BASECONFIG**: `baseConfig()` in `api/_lib.js` must ALWAYS initialize `secret: tokenSecret()` up front, never `secret: ""`! An empty secret in `baseConfig` caused cold-start lambdas to reject HMAC tokens with 401 Unauthorized before `loadConfig()` resolved.
- **HMAC TOKEN VERIFICATION**: Rely on cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 signature verification rather than strict `token_version` checking — when passwords change, derived secret flips and invalidates all old tokens automatically without bricking valid sessions across cold starts.
- **TELEGRAM BOT TOKEN EDITING & PERSISTENCE**: In the admin panel, the bot token is masked on GET and submitted blank if already saved. In `server.js` and `api/admin/_telegram.js`, always resolve `effectiveToken = botToken || prev.botToken` BEFORE checking `if (enabled && (!effectiveToken || !effectiveChatId))`. Checking raw `body.botToken` rejects saving when the user only changes `chatId` or toggles `enabled`.
- **TELEGRAM NOTIFICATION ON CONTACT FORM**: Contact submissions (`/api/admin/messages`) must call `notifyNewContactMessage` and log delivery status to `telegram-log.json` / `admin_settings` (`skipped: true` when disabled, `ok: true` on delivery, `error` on outage) without failing the public submission.
- **ANALYTICS & SESSION UNIQUE COUNTING**: In `_track.js` and `server.js`, `visits.days[today].visitors` array (session IDs) must be maintained to compute `todayUnique`, `totalUnique`, `last7Unique`, `last30Unique`, `thisMonthUnique`, and `thisYearUnique`. When Postgres / KV is configured, sync visits and clicks so stats survive serverless cold starts.
- **STATIC JSON REWRITE MAPPING**: In `api/index.js`, `STATIC_JSON` must map both `"site.json"` and `"site"` to `() => listData("site.json")` so public site data reflects admin changes dynamically.

# ProjectCard Logotype Pattern (working, user-approved)

File: `src/Page/Project/ProjectSection/ProjectCard/index.jsx`

## User corrections that shaped this (do not regress)
1. Screenshots/iframes rejected for preview area → pure logotype only.
2. Per-card gradient pool rejected ("Persian Persian Persian Persian Persian Persian") → ONE uniform brand gradient for all monograms.

## Key helper functions
```js
const getMonogram = (title) => {
  const words = title?.trim().split(/\s+/);
  if (!words || words.length === 0) return "?";
  if (words.length === 1) {
    const t = words[0];
    return t.length >= 2 ? t.substring(0, 2).toUpperCase() : t[0].toUpperCase();
  }
  return (words[0][0] + words[1][0]).toUpperCase();
};
```
- "Ubisoft" → "Ub"; "Sabz Learn" → "SL"; "Calculator" → "CA"

```markdown
# Sabz-Learn sub-project — structure, data inventory & sync workflow

Sabz-Learn is a SECOND Vite+React app embedded in the portfolio under
`public/Projects/Web-Project/Sabz-Learn/`. It has its own build, its own PHP
data backend, and is deployed in FOUR mirrored copies. Editing course data
without updating all four = stale data in one deployment.

## Layout
```
public/Projects/Web-Project/Sabz-Learn/
├── index.html            # entry; references ./assets/index-*.js (built)
├── .htaccess             # rewrites non-file paths to index.html
├── server/
│   └── data              # ★ STATIC data file the FRONTEND actually fetches
│                         #   (GET ${BASE_URL}server/data)
├── assets/               # deployed build output (mirror of all/dist)
│   ├── index-*.js|css
│   ├── Image/course-thumbs/*.svg   # 84 animated course thumbnails
│   └── server/db.json + index.php  # PHP backend reads THIS db.json
└── all/                  # source project
    ├── src/              # React source (Pages/Home, Pages/Courses, ...)
    ├── public/           # static assets; copied into all/dist on build
    ├── db.json           # ★ copy #1
    ├── server/db.json    # ★ copy #2 (dev PHP backend)
    └── dist/             # build output; mirrored into ../assets/
```

## The 4 data files (all must stay in sync)
| File | Who reads it |
|---|---|
| `all/db.json` | dev source / json-server |
| `all/server/db.json` | PHP backend in `all/` |
| `assets/server/db.json` | deployed PHP backend (base `/Projects/Web-Project/Sabz-Learn/`) |
| `server/data` | ★ the one the browser actually requests |

PITFALL: grepping only for `db.json` misses `server/data`. The frontend's
`fetch(${import.meta.env.BASE_URL}server/data)` hits the root `server/data`
file (a bare `{message, items, pagination}` object, no `data:` wrapper — while
the db.json files nest under a `data` key). Update all four, then verify LIVE:
`curl http://localhost/Projects/Web-Project/Sabz-Learn/server/data`.

## Changing course data / thumbnails (e.g. "one cover for all courses")
1. Copy the image into BOTH source asset trees:
   `all/public/assets/Image/course-thumbs/<name>.jpg` AND
   `assets/Image/course-thumbs/<name>.jpg` (the deployed one).
2. Rewrite every course's `thumbnail.url` to
   `./assets/Image/course-thumbs/<name>.jpg` in ALL FOUR data files.
   URLs are relative to the Sabz-Learn base URL.
3. Build the sub-app: `cd all && npm run build` (~3s).
4. Mirror `all/dist/*` → `assets/`  (`rsync -a all/dist/ assets/`).
5. Run the main portfolio build (regenerates `dist/` from `public/`):
   `cd <repo root> && npm run build` (~10s; >500 kB chunk warning is normal).
6. Sync XAMPP copy: image + all data files + `assets/` + `index.html` into
   `/c/xampp/htdocs/Projects/Web-Project/Sabz-Learn/`.
7. Verify LIVE from Apache (proves the served copy, not just files):
   - `curl http://localhost/Projects/Web-Project/Sabz-Learn/server/data` → all 84 thumbnails point at the new cover
   - `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" .../course-cover.jpg` → 200
8. Tell the user to hard-refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) — the SPA JS is hashed, but
   the JSON data is fetched at runtime so a cached page can linger.

## Notes / gotchas
- 84 courses. Thumbnails were regenerated once as animated SVGs (green
  gradient `#09733B→#27C85E`, sweep/glow/floatIn keyframes inline).
- Vite `base: "/Projects/Web-Project/Sabz-Learn/"` in `all/vite.config.js`.
- XAMPP data files use the same `data:`-wrapper vs bare-object split as above;
  parse with python using the right nesting.
- Python on this box cannot read bash-style `/c/xampp/...` paths — pass
  `C:/xampp/...` to python even inside a bash terminal.
```
