### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# Vercel Deployment Troubleshooting

## Overview

Common issues when deploying Vite/React/Next.js apps to Vercel, especially with Supabase or other backend services.

## Common Pitfalls

### Missing Environment Variables

The #1 cause of "works locally but broken on Vercel" is missing env vars.

**Why it happens:**
- `.env` is gitignored — it never reaches Vercel
- Vite injects `import.meta.env.*` values at **build time**, not runtime
- If Vercel has no env vars configured, the build compiles with `undefined` values
- The app falls back to a "setup notice" or crashes silently

**How to verify:**
1. Download the deployed JS bundle:
   ```bash
   curl -s "https://your-app.vercel.app/assets/index-*.js" > /tmp/app.js
   ```
2. Check for env var presence:
   ```bash
   grep -o 'YOUR-PROJECT\|demo-project\|your-anon' /tmp/app.js
   grep -o 'eyJ[A-Za-z0-9_-]\{20,\}' /tmp/app.js
   ```
   If you find `YOUR-PROJECT` or `demo-project` or nothing at all → env vars were not injected.

**The fix:**
- Go to Vercel dashboard → Project → Settings → Environment Variables
- Add all `VITE_*` vars (Supabase URL, anon key, etc.)
- Set to **All** environments (or at minimum **Production**)
- **Redeploy** — env vars are baked in at build time, so a redeploy is required after adding/changing them

### Supabase-Specific Gotchas

Projects using Supabase have a three-part setup:

1. **Supabase project** — create at supabase.com
2. **Database migration** — run `supabase/migrations/*.sql` in SQL Editor
3. **Vercel env vars** — `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` + `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`

If the app shows a setup notice or connection error, check all three in order.

### Build Cache Staleness

Vercel caches builds. After changing env vars, always click **Deployments → ⋯ → Redeploy** — a fresh deploy may still use old cached output.

### Framework Detection

Vercel auto-detects Vite from `package.json`. If detection fails:
- Add a `vercel.json` with build settings:
  ```json
  {
    "buildCommand": "npm run build",
    "outputDirectory": "dist",
    "framework": "vite"
  }
  ```

## Checklist for New Vercel Deployments

- [ ] `.env` is in `.gitignore` (don't commit secrets)
- [ ] `.env.example` has placeholder values that the code can detect
- [ ] All `VITE_*` vars are set in Vercel dashboard
- [ ] Migration SQL has been run in Supabase (or equivalent backend)
- [ ] At least one test user exists in the backend auth system
- [ ] Redeploy triggered after adding/changing env vars
- [ ] Deployed URL loads the actual app, not a setup notice

## Related Skills

- `systematic-debugging` — root cause methodology
- `dogfood` — exploratory QA of the deployed app


### 📚 Auxiliary References, Templates & Scripts

#### 📄 `references\supabase-vercel-case-study.md`

```markdown
# Vercel + Supabase Deployment Notes

## Session Case: porsyar (porskad)

**Symptom:** Deployed site at `https://porskad.vercel.app` showed:
> 🔌 Persian‌Persian Persian Persian Persian Persian Persian!

**Root cause:** `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` were not configured in Vercel Environment Variables.

**Why the `.env` file didn't help:**
- `.env` is in `.gitignore` — never pushed to GitHub
- Vite substitutes `import.meta.env.VITE_*` at **build time**
- Vercel built the app without those values → `isSupabaseConfigured = false` → SetupNotice renders

**Verification method:**
```bash
curl -s "https://porskad.vercel.app/assets/index-CbMuzcf_.js" > /tmp/app.js
node -e "
const fs=require('fs');
const js=fs.readFileSync('/tmp/app.js','utf8');
console.log('has demo-project:', js.includes('demo-project'));
console.log('has YOUR-PROJECT:', js.includes('YOUR-PROJECT'));
console.log('has setup notice text:', js.includes('Persian‌Persian Persian Persian Persian Persian Persian'));
"
```

**Fix:** Add `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` to Vercel dashboard → Settings → Environment Variables → Redeploy.

## Key Lesson

Vercel env vars are **build-time** injectables, not runtime. Changing them requires a redeploy to take effect. The `.env` file on the developer's machine is irrelevant to the Vercel build.
```

#### 📄 `references\telegram-serverless-rls-debug.md`

```markdown
# Debug Case: Telegram Send Works for Admin, Fails for Regular Users

## Project: porskad (React + Vite + Supabase, deployed on Vercel)

## Symptom
- Regular (anonymous) user submits a form → Telegram bot message is NEVER sent.
- Admin logged in (session token cached) → Telegram message sends correctly.
- `POST /api/telegram-send` executes in both cases; env vars claimed "correct".

## Root Cause — TWO stacked bugs

### Bug 1: public_id vs UUID mismatch in the embed path
- The public fill path (`/f/:slug` → `FormFill.jsx`) calls `sendToTelegram(form.id, ...)` with the **real UUID**.
- The embed path (`/embed/:formId` → `Embed/index.jsx`) called `sendToTelegram(formId, ...)` where `formId` came from `useParams()` — which is the **public_id** (`fr_...`), NOT the UUID.
- Server-side, `telegram_form_links.form_id` is a UUID FK. Querying with `fr_...` never matches → `links = []` → silent `skipped: true, reason: "no_telegram_link"`.

**Fix:** pass the real UUID from the embed RPC response (`schema?.uuid_id || formId`), and/or resolve `public_id → id` server-side in the API before the FK lookup.

### Bug 2: anon-key fallback + RLS = silent empty results
- `api/telegram-send.js` used `process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY || process.env.SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`.
- If the service role key is NOT set in Vercel env (only the VITE_* client vars are), the function runs as **anon**.
- Tables `telegram_config` / `telegram_form_links` have RLS policies allowing ONLY `admin`/`owner`. Anon role → RLS returns `[]` with **no error** → function believes "no link configured" and skips.
- Admin "worked" only because the admin's requests carried a valid session token; the serverless function itself never had one.

**Fix:** require `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (no anon fallback), fail loudly (500) if missing. Service role bypasses RLS for server-side ops.

## Also fixed along the way
- `entryNumber` off-by-one: `count(*)` runs AFTER the response insert, so it already includes the current response — display `entryNumber`, not `entryNumber + 1`.
- RLS errors (`linkError`, `configError`) were being swallowed into `skipped` — surface them in the JSON response and console.

## Verification method used
- `grep -rn "sendToTelegram\|telegram-send" src/ api/` to find ALL call sites and compare the identifier each passes (UUID vs public_id).
- Confirmed `get_public_form` RPC returns both `id` (public_id) and `uuid_id` (real UUID) — the embed already had the UUID available.

## General pattern (applies to ANY Supabase + Vercel integration)
1. When behavior differs between "logged-in admin" and "anonymous user", suspect (a) different code paths passing different identifiers, and (b) RLS + client role mismatch in serverless functions.
2. RLS denials return empty arrays, not errors — log/inspect the actual role the Supabase client runs as.
3. Serverless functions that touch RLS-protected tables must use the service role key; never fall back to anon silently.
```

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# Web & API Security Audit Mastery

Comprehensive, production-grade security auditing and hardening for Web Applications, REST/GraphQL APIs, Next.js Fullstack apps, and Node.js backends.

## 1. OWASP Top 10 & Web Vulnerability Audit Matrix

| Vulnerability | Attack Vector | Prevention / Hardening |
|---|---|---|
| **SQL / NoSQL Injection** | Unsanitized query concatenation | Parameterized queries (ORM, Prepared Statements), Zod schema validation |
| **Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** | `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, unescaped markdown | `DOMPurify.sanitize()`, Strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP), HttpOnly cookies |
| **CSRF** | Cross-origin state-changing POST/PUT | `SameSite=Strict` or `Lax` cookies, anti-CSRF tokens, Custom Header validation (`X-Requested-With`) |
| **SSRF** | User-supplied URLs fetched server-side | Private IP blacklisting (RFC 1918, `127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254`), DNS pinning, proxy egress |
| **IDOR / BOLA** | Tampering `userId` or resource ID | Session-bound authorization checks (`WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?`), RBAC middleware |
| **Mass Assignment** | Sending unexpected fields (`isAdmin: true`) | Strict DTO / Zod `.pick()` or `.omit()`, never spread `req.body` directly into DB |

## 2. Authentication & Session Hardening Checklist

### JWT Standards
- Store access tokens in memory or short-lived `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax` cookies.
- **NEVER** store JWTs in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` (vulnerable to XSS).
- Implement short lifespan (15m) + Refresh Token Rotation with DB revocation list.
- Verify algorithm explicitly (`algorithms: ['HS256']` or `['RS256']`) to prevent Alg=None bypass.

### Password Storage
- Hash with **Argon2id** (preferred) or **Bcrypt** (cost factor >= 12).
- Enforce constant-time comparison (`crypto.timingSafeEqual`) to prevent timing attacks.

## 3. Next.js App Router Security Pitfalls
- **Server Actions Exposure:** Server Actions are publicly callable HTTP POST endpoints. Always authenticate and validate inputs inside every Server Action.
- **Environment Variables:** Never prefix private secrets with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`.
- **Tainted Data:** Use React `experimental_taintUniqueValue` or `taintObjectReference` to block server secrets from leaking to client bundles.

## 4. HTTP Security Headers Configuration
Enforce standard security headers in `next.config.js` or Express middleware:

```javascript
const securityHeaders = [
  { key: 'X-DNS-Prefetch-Control', value: 'on' },
  { key: 'Strict-Transport-Security', value: 'max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload' },
  { key: 'X-Frame-Options', value: 'SAMEORIGIN' },
  { key: 'X-Content-Type-Options', value: 'nosniff' },
  { key: 'Referrer-Policy', value: 'origin-when-cross-origin' },
  { key: 'Permissions-Policy', value: 'camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()' },
  { key: 'Content-Security-Policy', value: "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-eval' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; font-src 'self' data:;" }
];
```

## 5. Security Audit Testing Workflow
1. **Source Code Review:** Check query construction, authorization checks, secret exposure.
2. **Fuzzing & Boundary Testing:** Pass unexpected types, payloads (`' OR 1=1 --`, `<script>`, `__proto__`, `../`).
3. **Auth Flow Inspection:** Verify token expiration, revocation on logout, rate limiting on `/login` and `/api/auth/*`.

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# WebRTC Mesh & Realtime Video Applications

Architecture, signaling patterns, stream lifecycle, UI UX pre-join flows, network resilience, and performance rules for client-side WebRTC mesh video and audio apps (up to 6-8 peers).

## 1. Signaling & Connection Orchestration

- **Deterministic Offer Initiator:** Prevent offer collision (glare) by assigning initiator role deterministically based on peer IDs (e.g. `isInitiator = myUserId > targetPeerId`).
- **Async Negotiation Serialization:** Wrap `createOffer()` with a per-peer `negotiating: Set<string>` guard. Because `createOffer()` and `setLocalDescription()` are asynchronous, rapid incoming signals or heartbeats will otherwise initiate concurrent duplicate offers while signaling state is still `stable`.
- **Automatic Renegotiation Wiring:** Always register `pc.onnegotiationneeded` to trigger offers when tracks are dynamically added or removed, and explicitly clear `pc.onnegotiationneeded = null` when calling `closePeer()` or `cleanup()`.
- **Hybrid Signaling Deduplication:** When pairing cloud signaling (e.g. Supabase Realtime) with local browser `BroadcastChannel` (for multi-tab dev/testing), tag every message with a unique `msgId` (`${userId}_${Date.now()}_${random}`) and drop duplicates via a bounded `Set<string>`.
- **Pre-allocate Transceivers:** Always create peer connections with `addTransceiver('audio', { direction: 'sendrecv' })` and `addTransceiver('video', { direction: 'sendrecv' })` before local media streams are acquired. This allows attaching tracks later via `replaceTrack()` without triggering SDP renegotiation loops.
- **ICE Restart Grace Period & Network Reconnect:** When a WebRTC connection drops into `disconnected` or `failed` (e.g. Wi-Fi flickers, mobile network switches), do NOT close the peer connection immediately. Trigger an automatic ICE restart (`pc.restartIce()`), send a new offer, and allow a 15-second grace window before closing. Register `window.addEventListener('online')` and `document.addEventListener('visibilitychange')` to immediately resubscribe signaling channels and send state updates when network/tab returns.

## 2. Audio & Video Stream Management

- **Mute/Unmute vs Track Lifecycle:** Toggle mic/camera mute by setting `track.enabled = false|true` on the existing stream track. Do NOT filter out tracks with `t.readyState === 'live'` in track sync loops if disabled tracks are still live — filtering them out causes track sync to treat muted tracks as missing and replace them with `null`, breaking transceiver state.
- **Dynamic Audio Constraint Toggling (Noise Cancellation):** Toggle AI background noise suppression, echo cancellation, and auto gain dynamically on active audio tracks using `audioTrack.applyConstraints({ noiseSuppression: enabled, echoCancellation: enabled, autoGainControl: enabled })`. This applies hardware/browser noise suppression live on-air without re-acquiring media streams.
- **The Duplicate Audio Phasing Trap:** When rendering a participant in both a main spotlight/screen-share view AND a thumbnail/carousel strip, NEVER mount `<audio>` elements in both components for the same stream. Pass `disableAudio={true}` to thumbnail tiles. Duplicate `<audio>` playback causes severe comb-filtering, echo, and volume distortion.
- **Speaking Detection Hysteresis:** Raw audio analyser frequency/RMS levels fluctuate rapidly between words and syllables. Debounce the transition from speaking to silent with a ~350ms timeout before setting `isSpeaking = false` and broadcasting signaling state. Never broadcast on every level tick.
- **Callback Ref & onLoadedMetadata Binding:** When rendering `<video>` or `<audio>`, unmounting elements during avatar placeholder states breaks `useEffect([stream])` bindings. Use a callback ref (`attachVideo = useCallback((el) => { if (el && stream) el.srcObject = stream; }, [stream])`) and attach `onLoadedMetadata={(e) => e.currentTarget.play().catch(() => {})}` directly on the JSX element so playback starts deterministically across Safari and Chrome.
- **Autoplay Gesture Recovery:** Remote `<audio>` `.play()` calls can be rejected by browser autoplay policies. Catch playback errors and register a one-time user gesture handler (`document.addEventListener('click', resume, { once: true })`) to recover audio.
- **Push-to-Talk Focus Safety:** When implementing Space-key push-to-talk, always register a `window.addEventListener('blur', releaseMute)` handler to automatically re-mute the microphone if window focus is lost while the key is pressed.

## 3. Screen Share & Track Sync

- **Reliable Sender Lookup:** Find peer senders via `pc.getSenders().find(s => s.track?.kind === 'video')` or `audio` rather than inspecting `transceiver.receiver?.track?.kind`, which can be unreliable or missing during media direction changes.
- **Clean Track Teardown:** Listen for native browser stop sharing via `screenTrack.onended`. When stopping, replace the peer video transceiver track with the current camera video track (or `null` if camera is disabled), and synchronously update both React state and its mutable `ref.current`.
- **Conserving Uplink Bandwidth:** When video is muted (`isVideoEnabled === false`), explicitly call `transceiver.sender.replaceTrack(null)` across all active peer connections instead of sending continuous black frames.

## 4. UI/UX Pre-Join & Avatar Patterns

- **Frictionless Direct Pre-Join Screen (Jitsi Pattern):** When a user navigates to a meeting URL containing a room ID (`/room-id`), bypass complex two-column room creation lobbies. Present a single centered pre-join card with a room title badge, media preview with in-box mic/cam toggles, display name input, and a single "Join Meeting" primary CTA.
- **Deterministic Avatar Color Algorithm:** When rendering fallback avatar placeholders, calculate background gradient colors deterministically from the user's name length and character code sum `(name.length * 7 + charSum) % gradients.length`. This gives each user a consistent, distinct avatar background that updates live as they type.

## 5. Session Lifecycle & Auto-Close

- **Auto-Close Empty Meetings:** Prevent zombie rooms by running a 30-minute idle timer when a meeting has 0 remote participants. Cancel the timer whenever a remote peer is connected. Pair this with a backend/database function (`auto_close_empty_rooms()`) or trigger on participant heartbeat to close stale abandoned rooms on the server side.

## 6. NAT Traversal & Relays

- **STUN + Multi-Protocol TURN Relays:** Pure UDP STUN servers cannot penetrate symmetric NATs, corporate firewalls, or restricted mobile carriers where UDP port 3478 is dropped. Always configure fallback TURN relay servers with multiple transport protocols (UDP, TCP on port 80/443, and TURNS over TLS on port 443: `turns:...:443?transport=tcp`).

## 7. Bandwidth & Bitrate Optimization (`setParameters` & `applyConstraints`)

- **Audio Bitrate Capping:** Constrain audio `RTCRtpSender` encodings to 32kbps (`params.encodings[0].maxBitrate = 32000`). This cuts audio bandwidth in half (~14-15 MB/hour) while preserving full Opus voice fidelity and active AI noise cancellation.
- **Screen Share Quality Presets:** Dynamically adapt screen share encoding parameters based on user workload:
  - *Low Data / Text & Code Mode:* 720p @ 15fps (`maxBitrate = 450000`, `maxFramerate = 15`) — cuts consumption to ~200 MB/hour (70%+ savings for code, slides, and docs).
  - *Balanced Mode:* 720p @ 30fps (`maxBitrate = 1200000`, `maxFramerate = 30`) — ~500 MB/hour.
  - *High Quality / Video Mode:* 1080p @ 30fps (`maxBitrate = 2500000`, `maxFramerate = 30`) — ~1.2 GB/hour.
- **Dual-Layer Quality Switching:** When switching quality presets mid-call, apply constraints to both the WebRTC sender encodings (`sender.setParameters(params)`) AND the active `MediaStreamTrack` (`screenTrack.applyConstraints({ width, height, frameRate })`) so the capture pipeline and network pipeline synchronize resolution and framerate immediately.

### ⚙️ YAML Configuration (`SKILL.md` Frontmatter)

```yaml
description: Use when building a Windows per-app cache cleaner app.

```

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# Windows per-app cache cleaner (CacheCleaner)

Project: `<USER_HOME>/Desktop/CacheCleaner/` — UI + CLI that lists every app's cache
with real sizes, shows what's inside each cache, and deletes it only after confirmation.

Interface is pywebview + `ui/index.html` (dark theme, Geist bundled in `ui/fonts/`), NOT tkinter:
see skill `pywebview-desktop-gui` for the bridge pitfalls. **English is the default language**
(README, launcher, report, test names, error messages), with a Persian switch in the header.
Persian strings live in `i18n_rules.py` + the `I18N`/`HELP` dictionaries in the page; the
choice persists as `config.json → lang`.

## Architecture (keep this split)

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `cc_rules.py` | per-app cache paths (env-var patterns, `*` allowed), English `kind` + `desc`, `risk`, `processes`, `PROTECTED_STRICT` / `PROTECTED_SCOPED`, `CACHE_DIR_NAMES`, `DISCOVER_ROOTS` |
| `i18n_rules.py` | `FA` dict keyed by the rule's English `app` name → Persian `app`/`kind`/`desc`; the scanner exposes them as `app_fa`/`kind_fa`/`desc_fa` on each `Target` |
| `scanner.py` | `dir_size` (scandir stack, tolerant of locks), `expand_glob`, `build_targets`, `discover`, `scan` (ThreadPoolExecutor 8), `drive_info`, `installed_apps` (uninstall registry via ConvertTo-Json), `pretty_pkg_name` |
| `cleaner.py` | `is_allowed` guard, `clean_target` / `clean_many`, CLI (`--list/--app/--all-low/--dry-run/--yes/--paths-file`) |
| `app.py` | GUI host: pywebview window + threaded API (`cc_start_scan`, `cc_scan_state`, `cc_entries`, `cc_apps`, `cc_start_clean`, `cc_clean_state`, `cc_open`, `cc_kill`, `cc_js_error`), UAC relaunch, `WINDOW = [None]` module holder |
| `ui/index.html` | whole interface: dark single-accent theme, tabs (Caches / Installed software), detail panel with per-entry breakdown, confirm + help modals, search/filter/sort, keyboard shortcuts |
| `report.py` | read-only CLI report with bar chart, `--json` |

## Safety rules (non-negotiable)

1. Delete cache **contents only** — never `rmtree` the cache folder itself, or apps break.
2. Three guard layers: `PROTECTED_STRICT` (never touch), `PROTECTED_SCOPED` (only sub-paths whose
   segment is in the allowed cache list, e.g. `Chrome\User Data\<profile>\Cache` OK, `Default\Login Data` no),
   and `cleaner.is_allowed()` (must be under an allowed root, not in the forbidden list).
3. `ALLOWED_ROOTS` normally rejects the root itself; keep an `EXACT_ROOTS` set for roots that ARE
   the cleanup target (`%WINDIR%\Temp`, `SoftwareDistribution\Download`, `Prefetch`).
4. Never put `%PROGRAMFILES%` / `%USERPROFILE%` / `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages` in PROTECTED_STRICT — they
   are parents of legitimate targets; use scoped protection instead.
5. Default everything to read-only; cleaning needs an explicit checkbox + confirm dialog; support `dry_run`.

## The scan animation (keep it honest)

- Feed the overlay from the running scan, never from fake timers. `scanner.scan()` takes a
  `tick(done, total, acc_size, acc_files, target)` callback fired from the pool workers;
  `cc_scan_state()` exposes `liveBytes`, `liveFiles`, `found`, `recent[]`, `currentFa`.
  The ring = done/total, readouts = the real accumulated numbers, the rail = one bar per
  measured location scaled to its real size, the ticker = newest caches found.
- `test_api.py` asserts `liveBytes == sum(target sizes)` after the scan; `test_gui.py` polls
  until the on-screen figure EQUALS the scanner's own total. A side-by-side single read can
  always be one poll behind, so assert convergence, not instant equality — and a test that
  reads the DOM and the API at different instants will flake.
- **`call()` must always return a Promise.** pywebview's JS bridge returns the raw value
  (a plain object, NOT a thenable), so `call("cc_scan_state").then(...)` threw
  `call(...).then is not a function` and the follow-up work silently never ran — the overlay
  stayed at 0. Wrap with `Promise.resolve(...)` and log JS errors (that is how this surfaced).
- Screenshot the animation mid-flight by sending the app's own `R` (rescan) shortcut with
  `SendKeys` and then bursting PrintWindow grabs; verify the burst really caught the overlay
  by checking the centre brightness/accent-green pixel count jumps, and that the percentage
  region's hash changes between frames.

## Closing the app / not lingering in the background

- Closing the window must end the process. `window.events.closing` sets an `EXIT` event the
  worker progress callback checks (raising out of a running scan), and after
  `webview.start()` returns, call `os._exit(0)` — non-daemon stragglers otherwise keep the
  process alive with no window. Daemon threads alone are not enough.
- **A duplicate launch is the real cause of "it is still running in the background"**: the
  second window hides behind the first, so closing the visible one leaves a live process.
  Guard with a named mutex. Two details decide whether the guard works at all:
  - `Local\Name`, not `Global\Name` — `Global\` needs SeCreateGlobalPrivilege, so
    `CreateMutexW` fails with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED for a normal user and the guard silently
    never engages.
  - Load it as `ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)` and read
    `ctypes.get_last_error()`; plain `ctypes.windll` does not preserve the last error, so
    `GetLastError()` returns 0 and the `ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS` (183) check never fires.
  - Do NOT show a MessageBox on the second launch: it blocks that process until someone
    clicks OK, leaving a stuck copy alive. Restore/focus the existing window and exit.
- Prove it with `test_shutdown.py`: launch → close via `CloseMainWindow()` → poll until the
  process AND its `msedgewebview2.exe` children are gone; then launch twice and assert one copy.

## Outbound links from the UI

- Never let the page pass a URL to the shell. Keep a fixed table in Python (`USER_LINKS`),
  look the key up, check the host against an allow-list, then `os.startfile(url)`.
- Keep a real `href` in the markup (so it still works outside the app) and `preventDefault()`
  in JS, calling the bridge instead — assert both: the click is cancelled AND the bridge got
  the right key AND `location.href` did not change.
- `evaluate_js` does NOT await promises in pywebview 6.x: an `(async () => {...})()` probe
  returns `{}`. Split such assertions into two synchronous evaluations with a `time.sleep`
  between them and stash the intermediate state on `window.__t`.

## Verified pitfalls

- **Never name the translate helper `t`.** The render loops already use `t` for the current
  target, so `t("key")` called the row object and threw `TypeError: t is not a function` —
  which silently killed the detail panel, row labels and help dialog. Use `T`, and rename in
  one regex pass (`\bt\("` → `T("`) rather than by hand.
- **Put translations in a side table keyed by the English name, never inline.** `test_i18n.py`
  then proves every rule has an entry, no entry is orphaned, no translation still equals the
  English source (which would look done but be untranslated), and the text really contains
  Persian characters. Brand names must keep their Latin spelling in both languages.
- **Bundle a real Persian font (Vazirmatn).** Geist has no Persian glyphs, so `dir="rtl"`
  silently fell back to a system face and the design broke.

- **Default the size floor to 25 MB and keep an escape hatch.** Hundreds of caches are tiny
  (a few KB); showing all of them buries the ones that matter. Blank must mean "no bound" and
  `0` a real value, so parse with a strict helper (`"" -> null`, `Number.isFinite`, `>= 0`)
  rather than truthiness — `if(!min)` breaks a legitimate 0. Offer a status-bar chip that clears
  both boxes so nothing is ever unreachable, and put the real byte size on each row
  (`data-size`) so a test can assert the range was actually applied instead of passing trivially.
- **PowerShell mangles Persian text** in both `-Command` and `-File`: `New-Object WScript.Shell`
  `CreateShortcut` with a Persian `.lnk` name fails with FileNotFoundException (path shows as `????`).
  Workaround: create the shortcut with an ASCII name, then `os.replace()` it to the Persian name.
  Write any helper `.ps1` as `utf-8-sig`.
- `powershell -Command` inside MSYS bash eats `$_`; write a `.ps1` file instead.
- Registry `EstimatedSize` is self-reported and often wrong — measure with a real scandir walk
  (~30 GB of caches on this machine vs registry claims). Full scan with 8 threads: 7–30 s.
- `scanner.py` must not import `cleaner` (circular); CLI helpers that need both live in `cleaner.py`.
- Registry keys are English but names/publishers can be Persian — never let encoding assumptions
  break the report (`sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8')`).
- Entry names with `\U` sequences in test files break Python string parsing — write test data with
  `write_file`, not through a heredoc / `python -c` one-liner.
- A leftover duplicate `call()` in the page's JS shadows the real dispatcher and every API call
  throws `ReferenceError` — the window renders but never populates. grep the file for the
  function name before blaming the Python side.
- `python` on PATH here is the Hermes venv (no pywebview); the GUI must be launched with
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Python\Python314\pythonw.exe`, which `CacheCleaner.bat` now probes for.

## Tests (all must print FAILURES: 0)

- `test_guard.py` — ~40 path cases + sanity check that no rule path is protected/disallowed.
- `test_clean.py` — real deletion on an artificial sandbox under `%TEMP%`, never real caches.
- `test_api.py` — the Python API the interface calls (scan state, entries, config persistence).
- `test_gui.py` — launches the real window and asserts on the live DOM via `evaluate_js`
  (rows rendered, fonts loaded, detail panel, checkbox selection, confirm dialog, apps tab,
  help, search filter, size band, no horizontal overflow, no JS errors). 50+ checks.
- `test_i18n.py` — rule ↔ translation parity, no untranslated/empty/orphan entries, Persian
  characters actually present, English rules stay English, brand names preserved.
- `test_shutdown.py` — closing the window leaves no process behind; a second launch does not
  start a duplicate.

Add a rule → run `test_guard.py` immediately; a new rule that hits a protected path fails there.

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# Windows GUI automation (pywinauto, no `computer_use` tool)

Use this when you need to operate a **native Windows app** (Telegram Desktop,
Discord, desktop chat/social clients, custom-drawn Qt/UWP windows) and the
`computer_use` tool is **not** in your toolset. This is the fallback path.
If the `computer_use` tool IS available, prefer it; this skill is for when it
isn't (check with `tool_search` first — don't assume).

## When it applies
- The user runs a desktop app (Telegram.exe, etc.) and asks you to work inside it.
- You found the app running, e.g. `tasklist | grep -i telegram`.
- The app is a **native/custom-drawn window**. Its UIA tree is often nearly
  empty (Telegram exposes only title-bar buttons, no chat widgets) — that is
  normal, not a failure. You still drive it via window title + keyboard/mouse.

## Dependencies (install once in the Hermes venv)
```bash
V="$HOME/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/venv"
VIRTUAL_ENV="$V" uv pip install pywinauto pyperclip
```
`pywinauto` and `pyperclip` are usually already present. Verify imports before
reinstalling. `uv` (not pip) targets the venv because naked `pip`/`python -m
pip` are often missing.

## Core workflow (title-signal + verify-before-typing)

1. **Connect** to the running process:
   ```python
   from pywinauto import Application
   d = Application(backend="uia").connect(process=PID)
   ```
2. **Enumerate visible windows and their titles.** The window **title text is
   your primary status signal** for named/custom apps (it shows the active
   chat/document name). Dump titles with `win.window_text()`.
3. **Navigate** by the app's own mechanism (a `tg://`-style deep link, a menu,
   a keyboard shortcut) and **confirm** the title changed to your target BEFORE
   doing anything destructive.
4. **Verify target == destination**, focus the right window, position the
   cursor, then input.

## The acute pitfalls seen in practice

- **String-match on titles breaks with non-ASCII dash.** Telegram Desktop titles
  use an **en dash** `–` (U+2013) between name and `– (NNNN)` — NOT ASCII `-`.
  A check like `"-" in title or t.count("(") >= 1` silently returns `False`
  FOREVER even when the window is right there. Match the **real target
  substring** (e.g. `"Saved Messages" in title`) or Unicode name, never the dash.
- **Don't type into a chatable app while the user is actively switching
  tabs/threads.** One wrong frame and a "message" of yours lands in the wrong
  chat (a group or another person). If the title keeps bouncing between
  different threads, STOP auto-typing: coordinate — ask the user to open the
  target chat themselves, confirm the title, then send. Never blind-send.
- **Pixel-coordinate clicks into custom-drawn composers often miss.** In
  Telegram Desktop a computed input click (e.g. `(left+300, bottom-30)`) +
  Ctrl+V + `{ENTER}` reported fine but the message **never arrived** — the
  click landed on a dead zone that stole focus, so paste/Enter went nowhere.
  The script's own "SENT" output is NOT proof of delivery: verify with the
  app's own state (title / UI) or have the user confirm. Prefer letting the
  app auto-focus the composer (opening/activating a chat usually does); treat
  coordinate math as a last resort.
- **`tg://`-style deep links navigate once, then silently no-op.** The first
  launch jumps to the target; while the app is already focused or the user is
  busy, re-running the same link often does nothing and the window keeps its
  current (possibly wrong) chat. Re-read the window title right before every
  send and confirm it is STILL your target — never assume a re-launched link
  re-navigated.

## Unicode (non-Latin) input
`pywinauto` `send_keys` can struggle with Persian/CJK. Reliable path:
1. `pyperclip.copy("Persian")`
2. `send_keys("^v")` (Ctrl+V paste)
3. `send_keys("{ENTER}")`
Every input is Ctrl+V of the (Unicode-safe) clipboard, not per-keystroke.

## pywinauto API traps (that you will trip on)
- `mouse.click(coords=(x, y))` sets **pixel coordinates** and has **no**
  `absolute=` kwarg. Calling `click(coords=..., absolute=True)` raises
  `TypeError`. Pixel coords are already absolute.
- `from pywinauto.keyboard import KeyboardInput` does **not** exist — use
  `from pywinauto.keyboard import send_keys`.
- `node.element_info.element_type` does NOT exist — UIA type is
  `node.element_info.control_type` (e.g. `Button`, `Edit`, `Group`).
- Connecting by PID then reading `top_window()` can return a transient title
  such as `'TelegramDesktop'` or a tooltip; iterate `d.windows()` and filter
  on `is_visible()` + the title you care about.
- Focus must be on the actual window: `win.set_focus()` before operating.
  Deep links may or may not bring it to front if the user is busy.

## Safety
- **Never** type/send/click into a chat, form, or dialog whose identity you
  have not verified (title != target). Ask the user to open the right screen
  if you can't get there reliably.
- **Never** read or dump the *content* of someone else's personal chats; you
  only need window titles and your own target. Reading a private chat body to
  "see" is a scope violation.
- Coordinate when the user is actively working in the same window, or do it in
  one tight pass with them standing by.

## Lighter alternative: PowerShell window activation (no pywinauto)
For "list open apps / bring window X to front / launch an app from the taskbar"
you often don't need pywinauto at all — a tiny PowerShell script does it:
- `Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.MainWindowTitle }` lists visible windows
  (and reveals the real process name when `Get-Process -Name <guess>` fails).
- user32 P/Invoke (`IsIconic`/`ShowWindow(SW_RESTORE)`/`SetForegroundWindow`)
  restores a minimized window; if the app isn't running, find its exe
  (`$LOCALAPPDATA` / Start Menu / Uninstall registry) and `Start-Process` it,
  then verify a titled window appears after ~5–8 s.
- **Pitfall (git-bash):** inline `powershell -Command "...$_..."` breaks — bash
  expands `$_`. ALWAYS write the script to a `.ps1` and run
  `powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File script.ps1`.
Full working scripts: `references/powershell-window-activation.md`.

For Telegram Desktop specifics (deep links, verifying Saved Messages, end-to-end
caveats), see `references/telegram-desktop.md`.


### 📚 Auxiliary References, Templates & Scripts

#### 📄 `references\powershell-window-activation.md`

```markdown
# PowerShell window activation & app launch (no Python needed)

For "list what's open", "bring window X to front", "open app X from the taskbar"
— when pywinauto is overkill or you just need to focus/launch a window fast.

## CRITICAL pitfall: bash mangles `$_` in inline PowerShell

Run from git-bash, `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.MainWindowTitle } ..."`
FAILS: bash expands `$_` to the last command's final argument (e.g. `/c/Users/<USER>`)
and PowerShell then errors `'/c/Users/<USER>.MainWindowTitle' is not recognized...`.

**Fix: always write the script to a `.ps1` file, then run it:**
```bash
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:/path/script.ps1"
```
Never inline PowerShell with `$_` through bash. (Single-line commands without `$_`
are fine inline.)

## List open windows (programs on the desktop)

```powershell
Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.MainWindowTitle -ne '' } |
    Select-Object @{N='Program';E={$_.ProcessName}}, @{N='Window';E={$_.MainWindowTitle}} |
    Sort-Object Program | Format-Table -AutoSize | Out-String -Width 200
```
Only processes with a visible window show up. This is also the way to discover
the REAL process name when `Get-Process -Name "<guess>"` returns nothing
(app window title ≠ process name, e.g. window title "Figma — project - Figma").

## Bring a running window to the foreground (user32 P/Invoke)

```powershell
$sig = @'
[DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool SetForegroundWindow(IntPtr hWnd);
[DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool ShowWindow(IntPtr hWnd, int nCmdShow);
[DllImport("user32.dll")] public static extern bool IsIconic(IntPtr hWnd);
'@
Add-Type -MemberDefinition $sig -Name Native -Namespace Win32

$p = Get-Process -Name "Figma" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $p) { $p = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.MainWindowTitle -like "*Figma*" } | Select-Object -First 1 }
if ($p) {
    $h = $p.MainWindowHandle
    if ([Win32.Native]::IsIconic($h)) { [Win32.Native]::ShowWindow($h, 9) | Out-Null }  # SW_RESTORE
    [Win32.Native]::ShowWindow($h, 5) | Out-Null   # SW_SHOW
    [Win32.Native]::SetForegroundWindow($h) | Out-Null
    Write-Output "OK - $($p.ProcessName) (PID $($p.Id)): $($p.MainWindowTitle)"
} else { Write-Output "NOTFOUND" }
```

## Launch an installed app that is NOT running

1. **Check first whether it's actually open** — `NOTFOUND` often just means the
   window is closed, not that the name was wrong. Re-list with the script above.
2. Find the executable:
   - `ls "$LOCALAPPDATA/<App>"` (Electron apps like Figma install under AppData\Local)
   - Start-menu shortcut: `find "$APPDATA/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs" -iname '*<app>*'`
   - Registry: query `HKCU:\...\Uninstall`, `HKLM:\...\Uninstall`,
     `HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\...\Uninstall` for `InstallLocation`.
3. Launch + verify:
   ```powershell
   Start-Process "<USER_HOME>/AppData/Local/Figma/Figma.exe"
   ```
   Wait ~5–8 s (Electron apps spawn multiple processes), then confirm a
   window with a real `MainWindowTitle` exists.

## User-behaviour notes (from practice)
- A taskbar app that the user can see may have its window **minimized** — the
  open-apps list still shows it; SW_RESTORE via the activation script brings it up.
- Don't relaunch if it's already running with a window: focus it instead.
```

#### 📄 `references\telegram-desktop.md`

```markdown
# Telegram Desktop (Windows) automation notes

Session-derived specifics for driving Telegram Desktop (`Telegram.exe`) with
pywinauto. Verified items are marked ✅; items that were only partially
validated are marked ⚠️ so a future agent does not treat them as proven.

## App structure (verified ✅)
- Process name: `Telegram.exe` (check with `tasklist | grep -i telegram`).
- The main window is a **custom-drawn Qt window**, class `MainWindow`.
  Its UIA tree is nearly empty: only title-bar buttons and empty groups are
  exposed — **no chat widgets, no message-input Edit**. Do not rely on UIA
  element names for chat navigation.
- The window **title** is the reliable status signal: it shows the active chat
  e.g. `'Persian Persian Persian – (73346)'` or `'Saved Messages – (73340)'`.
  Separator is **en dash `–` (U+2013)**, not ASCII `-` (see the SKILL.md pitfall).
- Persian/RTL chat titles come back **prefixed with a Unicode LRM mark**:
  `'\u200eMy Best Friend – (73398)'`. Substring matching is immune
  (`"Saved Messages" in title`), but exact-equality checks (`title == "…"`)
  silently fail — normalize or use `in`. English titles like Saved Messages
  are returned without the mark.
- `Application(backend="uia").connect(process=4516)` works. `d.windows()`
  returns several handles; filter on `win.is_visible()` and the title you
  actually care about (one returned window is a tiny clock/tooltip, another
  can be titled `'TelegramDesktop'`).

## Opening a specific chat with a deep link (verified ✅ once, ⚠️ repeatable?)
- `tg://saved` opens the user's **Saved Messages** chat (title becomes
  `'Saved Messages – (NNNN)'`).
- Launch from Python: `os.startfile("tg://saved")` or
  `subprocess.run(["cmd", "/c", "start", "", "tg://saved"])`.
- ⚠️ In one session it navigated on the first call, then stopped re-navigating
  while the user was actively switching between chats in the app (title kept
  bouncing between a group and a private chat). Do NOT assume the deep link
  reliably re-navigates under active user interaction — **always poll the
  window title until it matches the target chat** before any input.
- A working loop: repeat { fire deep link, sleep ~1.2s, read visible window
  titles, break when `"Saved Messages" in title` } up to ~8 attempts. The
  first successful attempt in-session took just one call.

## Typing a Unicode message (verified components ✅, end-to-end ⚠️)
1. `pyperclip.copy("Persian")` (Persian/Unicode-safe; pywinauto `send_keys`
   alone is unreliable for non-Latin).
2. `w.set_focus()` on the window whose title == target chat.
3. Try to focus the message composer. A guessed click near the bottom
   (`x = rect.left + 300`, `y = rect.bottom - 30`,
   `from pywinauto.mouse import click; click(coords=(x, y))`) is AT BEST a
   heuristic. ❌ **Observed failure (this class of flow was re-tested): the
   paste+Enter then claimed success, but the user reported the message did NOT
   arrive** — the click missed the composer (Telegram's layout varies), the
   paste went nowhere, and there was no error to catch. Do NOT treat that
   click formula as reliable, and do NOT report a send as successful without
   the user confirming they actually see the message (or a screenshot).
4. `send_keys("^v")`, sleep, `send_keys("{ENTER}")`.
- ⚠️ The complete "write into Saved Messages" flow was NOT confirmed end-to-end:
  in addition to the live-switching case below, a real attempt whose click
  missed the composer sent nothing. **Always gate on title == target before
  the paste+Enter, and if the user is actively using the app, coordinate with
  them first.** Never claim "sent" from the absence of an exception — verify.

## Hard rules for chatable apps (learned the expensive way)
- Never send text while the visible chat could be a group or a third party.
  One wrong frame => your message goes to that chat. Title check first.
- If the title keeps changing between reads, the user is actively using
  Telegram: stop driving and ask them to open the target chat; then you can
  detect the title and complete the send in a single pass.

## Related
- Sending messages/files to the user from the *bot* side is a different path
  (Bot API via the Hermes gateway) — this reference is only about driving the
  user's Telegram Desktop UI itself.
```

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# Bringing up a full Node stack on Windows without Docker

For repos that ship a `docker-compose.yml` but the machine has no Docker: install the backing
services as portable Windows binaries side by side, then drive the app's own scripts.

## 1. Read the repo before installing anything
- `package.json` engines/scripts, `.env.example` (every service + secret the app expects).
- A `pnpm-lock.yaml` plus a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` means the lock covers BOTH root and sub-packages
  (`packages: ['.', 'frontend']`): `npm install` in either dir resolves a DIFFERENT (broken) tree.
  Detect it, use pnpm, otherwise you fight phantom peer conflicts.
- Real example: `@nestjs/schedule@12` peer-requires `@nestjs/common@^11||^12` while root pins ^10 →
  `npm install` dies with ERESOLVE while the committed pnpm lock resolves it fine. Do NOT "fix" it
  with `--legacy-peer-deps`; that silently installs an unsupported Nest combination.

## 2. Getting the services (Iran-network reality)
- `docker`/`psql` absent → do not ask the user to install anything heavy first; try portable binaries.
- PostgreSQL via the zonky embedded jar is the reliable route when vendor CDNs are blocked:
  download `embedded-postgres-binaries-windows-amd64-<ver>.jar` from a China maven mirror
  (`https://maven.aliyun.com/repository/public/...` reaches ~250KB/s where get.enterprisedb.com is
  TLS-cut), then `zipfile` → inner `postgres-windows-x86_64.txz` → `tarfile` gives a full
  `bin/lib/share` server (initdb.exe, postgres.exe, pg_ctl.exe, locale + ICU files).
- Redis: `github.com/tporadowski/redis` release zip (direct from Iran, or via the socks proxy).
- MinIO Windows binaries are no longer served (dl.min.io answers 410 Gone, mirrors 404). Use a local
  S3 substitute such as `s3rver` (npm) instead of leaving the app in storage "fallback mode".
- npm registry: when `registry.npmjs.org` and `registry.npmmirror.com` both RESET, `mirrors.tencent.com/npm`
  and `mirrors.huaweicloud.com/repository/npm` serve metadata and tarballs. Put the mirror in the
  project `.npmrc` so the user's own `npm i` works too.

## 3. Server lifecycle on Windows (the part that wastes hours)
- **NEVER launch a server through `terminal` foreground.** `pg_ctl start`, `nest start`, and `npm run dev`
  keep the pipe open after printing, so a foreground call sits until the 180s timeout and you lose the
  output. Use `background=true` (with `notify=true` for bounded jobs), then poll the port/log in a
  separate call.
- The terminal harness also rejects `nohup`/`&`/`disown` wrappers and backgrounding with `&` — including
  one hiding inside a compound command. A `powershell Start-Process ... -RedirectStandardOutput` line
  that also does `sleep` + curl in the same command will be reported as a backgrounding attempt; split it.
- Anything that survives the agent (Postgres, Redis, the S3 shim) is most reproducible via
  `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Start-Process -FilePath <exe> -ArgumentList ... -WorkingDirectory ...
  -WindowStyle Hidden -RedirectStandardOutput <log> -RedirectStandardError <err>"` — run that as its own
  background call and verify by port.
- A Node script started by `terminal background=true` exits instantly with `stdin is not a tty`; appending
  `< /dev/null` fixes it. Same trick for `psql`/`redis-cli` waiting on stdin.
- Kill a server by owner PID, never by guessing: `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force"`
  with the PID from `netstat -ano | grep ":<port>" | grep LISTENING`.
- Hand the user a `START-<project>.bat` (checks each port with `netstat | findstr`, launches only what
  is missing, prints URLs + seed logins, opens the browser) and a matching `STOP-...bat`. Port-guarded
  starts make it idempotent, so double-clicking twice is harmless.

## 4. First-run bootstrap
- Generate real secrets into `.env` (never ship the `.env.example` placeholders: a missing 32-byte hex
  key makes crypto/blind-index code throw at runtime); `secrets.token_hex(32)` for hex-key vars.
- `npx prisma generate` before anything imports the client — `PrismaClient` throws
  "did not initialize yet" otherwise, and a generic `require('@prisma/client')` script will fail on it.
- `npx prisma db push` creates the database itself when absent, so no psql needed to CREATE DATABASE.
- Run the repo's real seed (`npx ts-node prisma/seed.ts`) and grep it for the seeded logins
  (`argon2.hash('...')`, admin phones) — those become the credentials you hand the user.
- Read `prisma/migrations/*.sql` for RLS: policies keyed on `current_setting('app.current_tenant_id')`
  mean a seed/script running outside a tenant context needs the platform-admin path, not raw inserts.

## 5. Prove it actually works (not just "port is listening")
- Screenshot-free UI verification: `puppeteer-core` against the installed Chrome
  (`C:/Program Files/Google/Chrome/Application/chrome.exe`), one `browser.createBrowserContext()` per
  account so logins do not leak between roles.
- **Drive the real login form** rather than injecting localStorage — you then also test the form, the
  axios interceptors, and the role redirect. Clearing a prefilled input needs
  `click()` + `Ctrl+A` + `Backspace`; `click({clickCount:3})` leaves the old value, and a doubled
  identifier makes the login 401 for reasons that look like wrong credentials.
- Treat the app's own rate limiter as a real obstacle: 5 failed logins lock the identifier AND the IP
  for 5 minutes (10 → 30 minutes). During harness debugging that is very easy to trip, and the lock
  survives in Redis. Clear it deliberately (`redis-cli --scan --pattern 'brute:*'` → `flushdb`) or
  restart the API, then confirm a fresh login returns 201 before blaming the credentials.
- Assert on rendered content, not shell: `document.body.innerText.length` plus the visible
  headings/table rows, and collect console errors and non-2xx `/api/` responses per page. A dark
  full-page screenshot proves nothing on its own, but a pixel-histogram of the PNG confirms the page
  is the themed app rather than a blank/error page.
- Exercise the storage path end to end (upload → GET the returned `fileUrl`) whenever the app has one;
  "fallback mode" in the startup log means you have tested nothing.
- Repair the local object store's health contract: the API probes `http://<endpoint>:<port>/minio/health/live`.
  A plain s3rver answers 404 there while uploads work fine — run s3rver on 9001 and front it with a tiny
  `http` shim on the MinIO port that answers that path 200 and proxies everything else, so the health
  endpoint reflects reality instead of a fake failure.
- Match credentials to the substitute: s3rver accepts only `S3RVER`/`S3RVER`. Any other
  `MINIO_ROOT_USER` yields `InvalidAccessKeyId` on every upload while the API still boots with only a
  warning ("Operating with fallback mode"), i.e. it fails quietly at the exact feature you are testing.

## Pitfalls
- Do not accept the startup log's "successfully started" as verification; the app happily runs with a
  dead DB/Redis/storage and serves 500s.
- Report frontend/backend contract mismatches you hit (e.g. a page calling `/finance/contracts/my-contract`
  while the controller only exports `my-overview`, so the page silently falls back to hardcoded mock data)
  as findings — the console 404 is the only signal; the UI looks fine.
- `@nestjs/schedule` and friends with build scripts need `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` (or `pnpm rebuild`)
  or their postinstall binaries stay missing.

### 📋 Skill Procedural Instructions & Workflows

# XAMPP PHP App Setup (Windows)

Get a PHP web app running under `C:\xampp\htdocs\<app>` on Windows, fully tested. The user (Persian-speaking) routinely drops projects here and asks: fix config, run XAMPP, create the database, test, then reports "tell me when to open the link".

## Workflow

1. **Inspect the project** — read `index.php`, `README.md`, `app/core/Database.php`, `app/config/config.php`, `database/schema.sql`. Note DB constants used (DB_HOST/NAME/USER/PASS/CHARSET), router behavior, and any `.htaccess` rewrite rules. README may be UTF-8 but the `read_file` tool can report it as "binary" — use `file README.md` + `cat` in terminal instead.
2. **Fix config.php for localhost**: `DB_HOST=localhost`, `DB_NAME=<snake_case_db>`, `DB_USER=root`, `DB_PASS=''`, `APP_URL=http://localhost/<app-folder>`, `APP_TIMEZONE=Asia/Tehran`. cPanel placeholders (`yourcpaneluser_*`, `CHANGE_ME`, `https://yourdomain.com`) are the giveaway that it's unconfigured.
3. **Start services as background processes** — see commands below. NEVER use `&` in a foreground terminal call (blocked); use `terminal(background=true)`.
4. **Create DB + import schema**: `mysql -u root -e "CREATE DATABASE ..."` then `mysql -u root <db> < schema.sql`. Check tables, seed rows, and Persian data.
5. **Test with curl**: page HTTP codes, then real login/register round-trips (CSRF-aware — see references file). Full flow: landing 200 → register → auto-login → dashboard 200 → admin login → admin dashboard 200.

## Exact commands (git-bash)

```bash
# MySQL (background)
cd /c/xampp && ./mysql/bin/mysqld --defaults-file=./mysql/bin/my.ini

# Apache (background) — MUST use absolute -d AND -f paths
exec /c/xampp/apache/bin/httpd.exe -d "C:/xampp/apache" -f "C:/xampp/apache/conf/httpd.conf"

# readiness probes (both can come up fast)
/c/xampp/mysql/bin/mysqladmin -u root ping   # "mysqld is alive"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost/   # not 000
```

## Pitfalls (all hit in practice)

- **Apache launch with relative `-f` fails**: `httpd.exe` resolves a relative config path against its own bin dir, so `-f ./apache/conf/httpd.conf` becomes `C:/xampp/apache/apache/conf/...`. Always pass absolute `-d "C:/xampp/apache" -f "C:/xampp/apache/conf/httpd.conf"`.
- **`error.log` contains stale entries from old runs** (old DB names, old file paths, old PHP fatals). Check the *new* tail timestamps + `tasklist | grep httpd` before concluding a problem; a successful start appends fresh "AH00455 configured -- resuming normal operations" lines.
- **Terminal blocks complex multi-command one-liners** (heredocs, chained grep/sed/curl pipelines with quotes). Fix: `write_file` the script into the cache dir and run `bash /path/script.sh`. Don't retry inline.
- **Persian/UTF-8 data shows as `?`** in mysql client output unless you pass `--default-character-set=utf8mb4`. The data is fine; it's a display artifact.
- **CSRF protection returns 500/"Persian Persian Persian"** on any POST without the form's token. Always do GET first → extract token → POST with it (full recipe in references).
- **Register/validation forms may need ALL required fields** — a failed POST returns HTTP 200 with re-rendered form + validation errors, not a redirect. If the DB shows no new row, check your POST payload field names against the controller before assuming the app broke.
- A `login` test can return 500 if the previous register auto-logged-in the same session cookie — that's a test artifact, not an app bug. Use a fresh cookie jar or skip re-login.
- **Router subfolder handling**: many apps strip the subfolder from the URI in the router (e.g. `dirname(SCRIPT_NAME)`), so an app in `/invoice-app` works at `http://localhost/invoice-app/` without extra vhost config. Verify with curl.
- **ZIP deliverables on Windows**: git-bash `/usr/bin/tar` is GNU tar — no `-a` flag, and `tar -a -cf out.zip` produces a TAR file named `.zip` that `unzip` rejects («End-of-central-directory signature not found»). Also `Compress-Archive` from bash can exit 1/2. Reliable recipe — Windows bsdtar, with NATIVE `C:/` paths (NOT `/c/`):
  `/c/Windows/System32/tar.exe -a -c -f out.zip -C "C:/xampp/htdocs" <app>`
  then verify: `unzip -l out.zip | tail -1` (shows file count) and `grep -E 'vendor/|fonts/'` to confirm support assets are inside.

## Handoff to user

Report: config.php changes, services running, DB name + table/seed status, test results table, the URL (`http://localhost/<app>`), and any seeded admin credentials found in schema.sql/README (warn if README recommends changing them).

## Support files

- `references/csrf-curl-testing.md` — CSRF-aware login/register test recipe (token extraction, cookie jars, expected status codes).
- `references/auditing-feature-coverage.md` — how to AUDIT an already-live app: coverage-checklist method (form→controller→model), hardcoded-string scan, seed verification, tooling fallbacks (`search_files` fails on Windows → grep; `read_file` flags PHP as binary → sed; mysql at `/c/xampp/mysql/bin/mysql.exe`), and the file:line report format.


### 📚 Auxiliary References, Templates & Scripts

#### 📄 `references\auditing-feature-coverage.md`

```markdown
# Auditing a XAMPP PHP App: Feature / Subscription / Admin Coverage

Sibling task to "setup": the user asks you to AUDIT an existing, already-live app
(e.g. plans/subscription/admin coverage) and report gaps with exact `file:line`,
without modifying files. Learned on Factorchi (`<USER_HOME>/Downloads/invoice-app`,
live at `http://localhost/invoice-app`, DB root/no-pass).

## Recipe

1. **Enumerate structure via terminal `ls -R`, not `search_files`.**
   On this Windows/MSYS box, `search_files(target='files', pattern='*.php')` returned
   `total_count: 0`, and content search failed with `rg: ... IO error ... such path
   (os error 3)`. Don't fight it — fall straight to bash:
   `ls -R app/controllers app/views ...` and `grep -rn --include='*.php' -E '...'`.
   paths (with or without leading `C:/`) both work.

2. **Expect `read_file` to flag real filesystems as "binary".**
   UTF-8/PHP files (esp. ones with Persian text or a BOM) sometimes come back as
   `is_binary:true` from the `read_file` tool, returning empty content. The README
   already captures this for README.md — it also happens for PHP views/models/controllers.
   Workaround: `sed -n 'START,ENDp' path.php` or `cat -v path.php` in terminal.
   (`cat -v` shows UTF-8 bytes as `M-...` escapes — fine for structure, prefer
   `sed` to see raw Persian.)

3. **Verify seeds via the XAMPP mysql binary, not `mysql`.** `mysql` is NOT on the
   git-bash PATH in my sessions — but it works at the full path:
   `/c/xampp/mysql/bin/mysql.exe -uroot invoice_app -e "SELECT ..."`.
   Add `--default-character-set=utf8mb4` or Persian shows as `?`.

4. **Coverage checklist method.** For "can admin edit every field X", trace
   form field → controller `validateInput()` → model `create()/update()` column
   list. A field can be "editable" while the model drops it (e.g. `is_free` never
   reached `INSERT`/`UPDATE`). Report each requested field as DONE/partial/MISSING
   with `file:line`. Pay extra attention to icon/color/description/boolean-toggles —
   these are the classic silent gaps.

5. **Hardcoded-string scan for "this page shows a fixed value instead of the DB value".**
   Grep app-wide for the display tokens AND their English/`-normalized` forms:
   `grep -rn --include='*.php' -iE 'unlimited|Persian|Persian|Persian|Persian'`. Then verify each
   hit is *actually conditional on* the DB field (`$p['monthly_invoice_limit'] !== null ?`)
   not a literal. Confirm the real DB value pulled in step 3 (e.g. free plan limit = 3)
   to judge whether a "unlimited" label is a real bug or correct (NULL = unlimited).

6. **Nav/dashboard coverage**: list controllers in `app/controllers/<area>/` and route
   registration in `index.php` (the `$router->get/post('/admin/...')` block), then the
   sidebar template. A feature can be routed+controlled but **not surfaced in the nav**
   (e.g. samples gallery only reachable via a button inside Settings). Report that as a
   coverage gap, not "missing".

## Output shape (user expectation)
Per-app structured report: a per-field DONE/partial/MISSING table with exact `file:line`
and a one-line fix per gap; note what you did NOT find (bug already fixed in current code)
as explicitly as what you did find. Do not modify files on an audit — report only.
```

#### 📄 `references\csrf-curl-testing.md`

```markdown
# CSRF-aware curl testing of a PHP web app

Many of this user's apps have CSRF protection (a hidden `csrf_token` field). Any POST without it returns HTTP 500 or "Persian Persian Persian (CSRF)". Recipe that worked:

## Pattern: GET form → extract token → POST with cookie jar

```bash
BASE="http://localhost/invoice-app"
JAR=/tmp/jar.txt
rm -f "$JAR"

# 1. GET the form (this also seeds the session cookie holding the CSRF token)
curl -s -c "$JAR" "$BASE/admin/login" -o login.html

# 2. Extract the hidden token. NOTE: match the FULL field name, e.g. "csrf_token".
#    A generic pattern like name="token" will NOT match "csrf_token".
TOKEN=$(grep -oiE 'name="csrf_token" value="[^"]*"' login.html | sed -E 's/.*value="([^"]*)"/\1/')
test -n "$TOKEN" || { echo "NO TOKEN"; exit 1; }

# 3. POST with token + credentials; on success you get a 302 redirect
curl -s -b "$JAR" -c "$JAR" "$BASE/admin/login" \
  --data-urlencode "csrf_token=$TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "email=user@example.com" \
  --data-urlencode "password=secret" \
  -o resp.html -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n"

# 4. Follow-up authed GET (session persists via jar)
curl -s -b "$JAR" "$BASE/admin/dashboard" -o dash.html -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n"
grep -oiE '<title>[^<]*</title>' dash.html
```

## Register flow (more fields)

Registration controllers often require ALL fields and re-render the form (HTTP 200, not a redirect) when any is missing — a 200 with validation text is NOT success. Inspect `AuthController`/model for required field names first. For an invoice app the vulnerable set was:
`name, email, phone, store_name, business_type, password, password_confirm`. Missing `store_name`/`business_type` alone causes a validation 200 and no DB row.

## Expected signs of success

- Login/register POST returns **302** (redirect), not 200/500.
- Follow-up dashboard GET returns **200** with the expected `<title>`.
- A new row appears in `users` (`SELECT ... FROM users ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1;`).

## Traps

- **Test-script greps failing silently**: token extraction returned empty twice because (a) the field is `csrf_token` not `token`, and (b) passing `--data-urlencode "_csrf=..."` (wrong name). Always verify the token variable is non-empty before posting; dump the `<input>` names if it fails.
- **Reuse of an already-logged-in cookie jar**: after a successful register (which auto-logs-in), a subsequent `login` POST on the same jar can 500. Use a fresh jar or don't re-login.
- **Complex inline bash with grep/sed/curl+quotes can be blocked by the terminal parser** ("command parser limit or malformed executable payload"). Write the whole test as a script file (`write_file`) and run `bash /path/script.sh`. Retrying inline unchanged does not help.
```

#### 📄 `references\deploy-and-seed-gotchas.md`

```markdown
# Deploy, seed-file, and handoff gotchas (hit while finalizing Factorchi on XAMPP)

## Deliverable seed SQL (MariaDB has no `--add-comments`)
`mysqldump --add-comments` is an unknown option on this MariaDB. Build the clean seed:
```bash
/c/xampp/mysql/bin/mysqldump.exe -uroot --no-create-db --skip-comments \
  --default-character-set=utf8mb4 <db> > raw.sql
{ echo "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS <db> CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_ci;";
  echo "USE <db>;"; cat raw.sql; } > database/<app>_final.sql
```
Verify on a COPY: `sed 's/<db>/<db>_verify/g' final.sql > v.sql` → import with
`mysql -uroot < v.sql` → count tables + seed rows → `DROP DATABASE <db>_verify`.
Never "verify" by re-importing into the live DB, and don't forget the embedded
`USE <db>;` means import time always goes into the real DB name (only the sed'ed copy
proves portability). The header makes the file safe to hand to `mysql -uroot < file`.

## Junction → real folder (final deployment on user request "Persian Persian Persian XAMPP/htdocs")
- `rm -d /c/xampp/htdocs/<app>` removes ONLY the junction link (MSYS).
- `mv` after that failing with "Device or resource busy": (a) cd out of the source
  folder first — a stale shell cwd inside the source pins it; (b) Explorer window
  open on the folder pins it too — keep the copy, tell the user to close the window.
- `cp -r` + `diff -rq` still work even when rename/delete is pinned; after any move,
  prove serving with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost/<app>/`.
- Remove-Item -Force on a junction from PowerShell sometimes acts on the TARGET —
  `rm -d` via MSYS bash was the reliable link-only removal.

## Audible sign-off
`[console]::beep()` works from PowerShell; System.Media/SoundPlayer does NOT exist here
(Add-Type assembly not found) — skip SoundPlayer entirely. Play beeps as the last step:
`[console]::beep(1200,180); Start-Sleep -m 80; [console]::beep(1600,500)`.

## Stale-browser-session crashes (classic localhost PHP)
DB wiped (user deleted / clean seed) but the browser still holds the old session cookie
→ app errors (FK/user 404 or "logged-in" ghost states). Clear BOTH halves:
- server: re `rm -f /c/xampp/tmp/sess_*`
- browser: the sqlite cookie delete described in the chrome-browser-automation skill
   (Cookies DB at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Network\Cookies,
    host_key LIKE '%localhost%').
```

#### 📄 `references\persian-font-embedding.md`

```markdown
# Persian font embedding (self-hosted, no CDN)

User wants a modern beautiful Persian font BUNDLED inside the project (works
offline). Verified on Factorchi (invoice-app) and study-tracker.

## 1. Find installed fonts
Persian fonts usually live in the per-user font dir, not C:\Windows\Fonts:
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts` (e.g. `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts`)
- Glob: `find /c/Windows/Fonts /c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts -iname "*vazir*" -o -iname "*morabba*" -o -iname "*iransans*" -o -iname "*yekan*" -o -iname "*ravi*"`

## 2. Pick the font (user preference order learned)
User asked for beautiful + MODERN, explicitly NOT Persian/Persian/Persian (no
old IRANSans/Faraz/BYekan look):
- **Ravi** (Persian) — the user's current preference; modern geometric, installed on Windows at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Fonts\`. Weights available: Regular (400), SemiBold (600), Bold (800).
- **Vazirmatn** (Persian Persian) — first choice historically; geometric, clean, available in full weight family (Thin..Black). ~123KB per TTF weight.
- IRANSansX — the new-gen IRANSans (acceptable, more "sans-serif standard").
- Old IRANSans / B Yekan / Tahoma — reject as old/official.
- If nothing good on disk, tell the user the font NAME to download — don't
  silently ship a bad font.

## 3. Embed
```bash
mkdir -p fonts
F="/c/Users/<user>/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Windows/Fonts"
# For Ravi:
cp "$F/Ravi-Regular.ttf" "$F/Ravi-SemiBold.ttf" "$F/Ravi-Bold.ttf" fonts/
# For Vazirmatn:
cp "$F/Vazirmatn-Regular.ttf" "$F/Vazirmatn-Medium.ttf" "$F/Vazirmatn-SemiBold.ttf" \
   "$F/Vazirmatn-Bold.ttf" "$F/Vazirmatn-ExtraBold.ttf" fonts/
```

Replace CDN @font-face blocks in style.css with local ones:
```css
@font-face { font-family:'Ravi';src:url('./fonts/Ravi-Regular.ttf') format('truetype');font-weight:400;font-style:normal;font-display:swap; }
@font-face { font-family:'Ravi';src:url('./fonts/Ravi-SemiBold.ttf') format('truetype');font-weight:600;font-style:normal;font-display:swap; }
@font-face { font-family:'Ravi';src:url('./fonts/Ravi-Bold.ttf') format('truetype');font-weight:800;font-style:normal;font-display:swap; }
```
(font-weight 400/600/800 for Regular/SemiBold/Bold.)

**CRITICAL**: Each `@font-face` must be a SEPARATE declaration — DO NOT stack
multiple `src` URLs in one `@font-face` block. Also ensure `font-weight` matches
the actual file weight; mismatched weights cause the browser to skip the font.

## 4. Verify
- `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8765/fonts/Ravi-Regular.ttf` → 200
- Rebuild the deliverable ZIP afterwards (`Compress-Archive -Force`) and
  `unzip -l` to confirm fonts are inside.

## Jalaali date conversion (offline, no CDN)
For offline/production use, replace the jalaali-js CDN with a bundled function:
```js
function gregorianToJalali(gy, gm, gd) {
  const g_d_m = [0,31,59,90,120,151,181,212,243,273,304,334];
  let jy;
  if (gy <= 1600) { jy = 0; gy -= 621; } else { jy = 979; gy -= 1600; }
  const gy2 = (gm > 2) ? (gy + 1) : gy;
  let days = (365 * gy) + Math.floor((gy2 + 3) / 4) - Math.floor((gy2 + 99) / 100) + Math.floor((gy2 + 399) / 400) - 80 + gd + g_d_m[gm - 1];
  jy += 33 * Math.floor(days / 12053); days %= 12053;
  jy += 4 * Math.floor(days / 1461); days %= 1461;
  if (days > 365) { jy += Math.floor((days - 1) / 365); days = (days - 1) % 365; }
  const jm = (days < 186) ? 1 + Math.floor(days / 31) : 7 + Math.floor((days - 186) / 30);
  const jd = 1 + ((days < 186) ? (days % 31) : ((days - 186) % 30));
  return [jy, jm, jd];
}
const JALALI_MONTHS = ['Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian','Persian'];
function jalaliDateLabel(ts) {
  const d = new Date(ts * 1000);
  const [jy, jm, jd] = gregorianToJalali(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth() + 1, d.getDate());
  return `${toP(jd)} ${JALALI_MONTHS[jm-1]} ${toP(jy)}`;
}
function toP(str) { return String(str).replace(/\d/g, d => 'Persian'[d]); }
```
This eliminates the jalaali-js CDN dependency entirely.

## UI principle (live preview)
When a page needs «Persian‌Persian Persian» of the final output (invoice/PDF), render
the preview with the SAME markup + CSS classes as the real printable output
(e.g. `.invoice-paper.tpl-*`), not a parallel imitation. Then preview always
mirrors the final result by construction; switching the template class on the
preview container is the entire template-switch logic.
```
